issues.original: b) When defining component types by extending more than one parent type, there shall be no name clash between the definitions of the different supertypes, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).
issues.issue: Templates are omitted from the list of definitions; 'parent type' is used for supertype.
readings: A port, variable, constant, timer or template identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.
Only port, variable, constant and timer identifiers SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.

issues.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be applied directly to an array of component references.
issues.original: The configuration operations (see clause 21) do not work directly on arrays of components.
issues.issue: 'arrays of components' is used, but TTCN-3 only has arrays of component references.

issues.canonical: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
issues.original: a) The only operations allowed on component references are assignment, equality and non-equality.
issues.issue: 'operations' is read as expression operators; component operations such as start, stop, done or running are also applied to component references and are defined in clause 21, so a literal reading would contradict them.
readings: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
No operation other than assignment, equality and non-equality (including component operations like `start` or `done`) SHALL be applied to a component reference.

issues.canonical: The actual data representation of the address type IS resolved by an explicit global `address` type definition in the test suite, by address type declarations in port type definitions, or externally by the test system when `address` is left as an open type.
issues.original: The actual data representation of the global address type is resolved either by an explicit global address type definition within the test suite, address type definitions within port definitions, or externally by the test system (i.e. the address type is left as an open type within the TTCN-3 specification).
issues.issue: The sentence speaks of the representation of the 'global address type' being resolved by 'address type definitions within port definitions'; the chosen reading is that it describes the three ways the address representation in general is determined.
readings: The actual data representation of the address type IS resolved by a global `address` type definition, by address declarations in port type definitions, or externally by the test system.
The actual data representation of the global `address` type IS resolved by a global definition, or, if missing, by port-type address declarations or externally.

issues.canonical: If both a global `address` type definition and port type definitions with an address declaration exist in a module, the global address type SHALL only apply to ports whose port type has no explicit address declaration.
issues.original: If both a global address type definition and port definitions with an address type definition exist in a module, the global address type shall only affect ports without an explicit address type definition.
issues.issue: 'port definitions' is used where port type definitions are meant.

issues.canonical: A test suite SHOULD consistently use explicit address declarations in port type definitions rather than a global `address` type definition.
issues.original: The consistent use of explicit address type definitions within port definitions is recommended over the use of global address type definitions.
issues.issue: 'port definitions' is used where port type definitions are meant.

issues.canonical: For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.
issues.original: b) For addressing purposes, the address type shall only be used in the to, from and sender parts of receive and send operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.
issues.issue: Only 'receive and send operations' are named; procedure-based operations (call, getcall, reply, raise, ...) also have to/from/sender parts. The chosen reading treats receive and send as representatives of all communication operations.
readings: For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.

For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations, and in no other operation, of ports mapped to the test system interface.

issues.canonical: A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS written as the `length` keyword followed by a single value or a range with inclusive boundaries in parentheses, placed between the `record` or `set` keyword and the `of` keyword.
issues.original: The length keyword followed by a value or a range (with inclusive boundaries only) within brackets and used between the record or set and the of keywords, restricts the allowed number of elements for the given record of or set of type.
issues.issue: 'brackets' is used for the parentheses enclosing the length value or range.

issues.canonical: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
issues.original: For partial (i.e. incomplete) values, all following rules on templates apply.
issues.issue: 'all following rules on templates' can refer to the rules stated next in this clause or to the general template rules of clause 15; the first reading is chosen because of the word 'following'.
readings: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, all rules on templates of the core language (clause 15) SHALL apply.

issues.canonical: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
issues.original: When constraining `record of`, `set of`, `union`, `map` and `anytype` types, and arrays, all templates of the expanded list (i.e. after resolving the subtype references) shall be valid (i.e. complete) values and templates of the core type.
issues.issue: 'valid (i.e. complete) values and templates' leaves open whether matching mechanisms are allowed or only specific values; the reading allowing complete templates is chosen.
readings: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every element of the expanded list SHALL be a complete specific value of the core type.

issues.canonical: When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using assignment notation MAY be a partial template of the core type.
issues.original: When constraining `record` and `set` types, templates of the expanded list defined using the value list notation shall be valid (i.e. complete) templates of the core type, while templates of the expanded list defined using the field assignment notation may be partial (i.e. incomplete) templates of the core type.
issues.issue: 'field assignment notation' is used instead of the glossary term 'assignment notation'.

issues.canonical: A list subtype of an enumerated type SHALL contain only values of the parent type.
issues.original: In case of `enumerated` types, the template list subtyping shall contain only values of the parent type.
issues.issue: 'template list subtyping' is used instead of 'list subtyping'.

issues.canonical: Constants, variables and formal parameters of timer type MAY be defined.
issues.original: TTCN-3 allows to define timer constants, variables and parameters.
issues.issue: 'parameters' is used where formal parameters are meant.

issues.canonical: A timer reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance where the timer is defined.
issues.original: Timer references have meaning only within the test component instances where the timer is defined, i.e. a timer reference assigned to a timer variable in a test component instance "a1" of type "A" has no meaning in a test component instance "a2" of type "A".
issues.issue: The consequence of using a timer reference in another test component instance (error, or unspecified behaviour) is not stated.
readings: Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined causes a dynamic error.
Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined has unspecified behaviour.

issues.canonical: A map type IS a type that maps a set of unique keys to a set of values such that each key is associated with exactly one value.
issues.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of map types that map from a set of unique keys to a set of values in such a way that each value in the set of key is associated with exactly one value in the set of values.
issues.issue: The sentence says 'each value in the set of key is associated with exactly one value'; the intended meaning is 'each key in the set of keys'.

improper_terms.used: each value in the set of key
improper_terms.proper: each key in the set of keys

issues.canonical: A map value MAY be denoted with the index assignment notation.
issues.original: Values of the map type can be denoted with the indexed assignment notation where the indices are values of the key type of the map type and the right hand sides are values of the value type.
issues.issue: The text says 'indexed assignment notation' while the restriction of the same clause and clause 6.2.15.4 use 'index assignment notation'.

issues.canonical: A map template MAY use a mixed notation in which the first item is an asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments.
issues.original: Templates of the map type can use a specific form of the mixed notation, where the first item is and asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments (see clause B.1.3.2 for more details).
issues.issue: The prose requires 'one or more' indexed assignments after the asterisk, but the syntactical structure { ... } allows zero or more. The prose reading is used in the canonical text.
readings: A map template MAY use a mixed notation consisting of an asterisk followed by one or more indexed assignments.
A map template MAY use a mixed notation consisting of an asterisk followed by zero or more indexed assignments, i.e. { * } alone is valid.

issues.canonical: The `unmap` statement MAY be used to remove the mapping of a key to its associated value from a variable of a map type.
issues.original: To remove a mapping from a key to its associated value in a variable of a map type, the unmap statement may be used.
issues.issue: Clause 6.2.15.3 calls it 'unmap statement' while the next sentences and the NOTE in 6.2.15.9 call it 'unmap operation'; 'unmap operation' also names the port unmap operation.

issues.canonical: The ValueRef of an `unmap` statement SHALL be an initialized variable (or template variable) of a map type.
issues.original: a) ValueRef shall be an initialized variable of map type and SingleExpression shall be a value compatible with the key type of the map type of ValueRef.
issues.issue: The restriction says 'variable of map type', but the semantic description also allows map template variables; it is unclear whether a template variable satisfies the restriction. The reading that includes template variables is used.
readings: The ValueRef of an unmap statement SHALL be an initialized variable or template variable of a map type.
The ValueRef of an unmap statement SHALL be an initialized (value) variable of a map type; template variables are only allowed with the asterisk form.

issues.canonical: The index notation used on the right hand side with a key that has no associated value SHALL result in a test case error.
issues.original: c) An index notation used on the right hand side with a key that has no associated value shall result in an error.
issues.issue: The restriction says 'an error'; the example clarifies that a test case error (runtime) is meant.

issues.canonical: The value (`to`) type of a map type MAY be a record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map type.
issues.original: The usage of structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) is allowed.`
issues.issue: It is unclear whether the permission of structured types applies only to the 'to' part (as the preceding sentence says) or also to the key type (the NOTE implies structured keys are allowed but discouraged). The 'to'-only reading is used here.
readings: The value (to) type of a map type MAY be a structured type.
Both the key (from) type and the value (to) type of a map type MAY be structured types.

issues.canonical: A key IS removed from a map by the `unmap` operation (not by assigning `omit`).
issues.original: NOTE: The unmap operation is used for removing a key from a map.
issues.issue: The NOTE calls it 'unmap operation' while clause 6.2.15.3 calls it 'unmap statement'; 'unmap operation' also denotes the port unmap operation.

issues.canonical: A value field associated with a key of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, including `omit`, `*` and `ifpresent`.
issues.original: Value fields associated with keys of map templates might contain matching symbols including symbols for optional fields such as omit, * or ifpresent (see Annex B for more details).
issues.issue: 6.2.15.9-s002 forbids assigning omit to a map value field, while this sentence allows omit, * and ifpresent in map template value fields; also 'might' can be read as permission or as possibility. The permission reading for templates is used.
readings: A value field of a map template MAY contain omit, * or ifpresent.
A value field of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, but omit (and therefore * / ifpresent with omit semantics) is excluded by the prohibition of omit for map value fields.

issues.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used as the type of a formal parameter of a template, testcase, altstep, non-external function, map operation or unmap operation.
issues.original: Formal parameters of templates, test cases, altsteps, non-external functions, map and unmap operations
issues.issue: 'map and unmap operations' may denote the port map/unmap operations (which have a param clause) or the map type unmap statement of clause 6.2.15.3. The port operation reading is used.
readings: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the param clause of the port map and unmap operations.
The open type SHALL NOT be used as an argument type of the unmap statement on map variables (clause 6.2.15.3).

issues.canonical: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the type of the target or of the other operand.
issues.original: Generally, TTCN-3 requires type compatibility of values at assignments, instantiations and comparison.
issues.issue: 'Generally' implies exceptions without listing them here; the exceptions (strong typing) are given in clause 6.3.4. Chose the reading that type compatibility is the default rule.
readings: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type, except where clause 6.3.4 requires strong typing.
A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type in all cases.

issues.canonical: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
issues.original: The type of the formal parameter, which is to obtain the actual value of value "b" is called type "A".
issues.issue: Type "A" is defined only as the type of a formal parameter, but the rules of clause 6.3 also apply to assignments and comparisons. Chose the wider reading.
readings: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b".
Type "A" IS only the type of the formal parameter that obtains value "b".

improper_terms.proper: target object (formal parameter, variable, template variable, field)

issues.canonical: A value "b" of record type "B" IS compatible with record type "A" if the number and the optionality of the fields in textual order of definition are identical, the types of corresponding fields are compatible, and the value of each present field of value "b" is compatible with the type of the corresponding field in type "A".
issues.original: record types are compatible if the number, and optional aspect of the fields in the textual order of definition are identical, the types of each field are compatible and the value of each existing field of the value "b" is compatible with the type of its corresponding field in type "A".
issues.issue: 'the types of each field are compatible' does not say whether field types need only the same root type or must be compatible including subtyping; EXAMPLE 1 accepts AType (field a(0..10)) and BType (field a integer), so the root-type reading was chosen. Field names are irrelevant (EXAMPLE 1, CType).
readings: Corresponding field types SHALL resolve to the same root type; subtype violations are checked on the field values of value "b".
Corresponding field types SHALL be compatible including their subtype constraints.

issues.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use the default-alternative compatibility rules only if the rule based on identically named alternatives has not determined compatibility.
issues.original: The second rule shall only be used to check compatibility, when - using the first rule - no compatibility has been determined.
issues.issue: 'The second rule' is singular, but the 'Otherwise' bullet contains two default-alternative rules (union-to-arbitrary and arbitrary-to-union). Chose the reading that both are meant.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use both default-alternative rules only if the identical-alternative rule has not determined compatibility.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use only the union-to-arbitrary default-alternative rule as fallback; the arbitrary-to-union rule applies independently.

issues.canonical: A value of an open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment IS compatible with type "A" if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with type "A".
issues.original: Values of open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment are compatible with a value "a" of a type "A", if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with "A".
issues.issue: The rule says the open type value is compatible 'with a value "a" of a type "A"'; compatibility is defined between a value and a type, not between two values.

improper_terms.used: compatible with a value "a" of a type "A"

issues.canonical: If the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running MTC, a runtime error CAN occur.
issues.original: If the type of the mtc is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running mtc.
issues.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when a function with an `mtc` clause of type "A" is called in a context whose running MTC is not mtc-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error (or undefined behaviour) in that situation.

issues.canonical: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on, a runtime error CAN occur.
issues.original: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on.
issues.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when the system is not system-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error in that situation.

issues.canonical: For component type compatibility, a component template in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers, types, formal parameter lists and assigned template or template field values.
issues.original: d) For local template definitions, the identifiers, the types, the formal parameter lists and the assigned template or template field values shall be identical.
issues.issue: 'local template definitions' means templates declared in the component type, which the glossary calls component templates.

issues.canonical: The communication operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.
issues.original: The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.
issues.issue: The list omits `catch` (and `check`), while 6.3.4-s003/s004 treat `catch` like `raise`. Chose the literal list.
readings: Only the listed operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing.
All communication operations of clause 22, including `catch` and `check`, SHALL apply strong typing.

issues.canonical: The automatic type MAY be used only in a variable declaration, a template variable declaration, a constant declaration or a module parameter declaration.
issues.original: Automatic types are used in variable, constant and module parameter declarations.
issues.issue: The sentence is descriptive; it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive (other declarations, e.g. formal parameters or templates, are excluded) and whether template variable declarations count as variable declarations (the examples use `var template`). Chose the exhaustive reading including template variables.
readings: The automatic type MAY be used only in variable (including template variable), constant and module parameter declarations.
The automatic type MAY be used at least in variable, constant and module parameter declarations; other uses are not addressed.

issues.canonical: The type of the expression or template body used for automatic typing SHALL be unambiguously determinable from the expression or template body itself.
issues.original: The type of the expression or template body used for automatic typing shall be implicitly unambiguous.
issues.issue: "implicitly unambiguous" is not defined; it can mean determinable without any type context, or determinable according to the list a) to q). Chose the first reading, which the list then makes concrete.
readings: The type of the expression or template body SHALL be determinable without any external type context.
The type of the expression or template body SHALL be determinable by applying the rules of items a) to q) of clause 6.5.

issues.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a reference to an existing variable, formal parameter, constant or template, or to a field or element inside of it.
issues.original: a) Reference to an existing variable, parameter, constant, template or a field or element inside of it.
issues.issue: "parameter" is used where formal parameter (or module parameter) is meant.

issues.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a TTCN-3 operation returning a value, such as `match`, `valueof` or `ispresent`.
issues.original: c) TTCN-3 operation returning a value such as match, valueof, present, etc.
issues.issue: "present" is not a TTCN-3 operation; the `ispresent` operation is meant. The list is open ("etc.").

issues.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be a literal of the `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring` or `verdicttype` type.
issues.original: e) Literal of the integer, float, boolean, bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, verditctype type.
issues.issue: Typo "verditctype" for the `verdicttype` type.

issues.canonical: An assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the assignment notation.
issues.original: j) Field assignment notation where all values fulfil requirements for automatic typing shall provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the field assignment notation.
issues.issue: "field assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "assignment notation".

issues.canonical: Each value in an assignment notation used for automatic typing SHALL fulfil the requirements for automatic typing.
issues.original: j) Field assignment notation where all values fulfil requirements for automatic typing shall provide an automatic record type with the same number and order of fields as in the field assignment notation.
issues.issue: "field assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "assignment notation".

issues.canonical: An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes are of the `integer` type and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `record of` the common type.
issues.original: k) Index assignment notation where all indexes are of the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type record of _{common type}.
issues.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

issues.canonical: An index notation used for automatic typing in which all indexes have a common type other than `integer` and all item values have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `map from` the common index type `to` the common value type.
issues.original: l) Index assignment notation where all indexes have a common type in case the type is different from the integer type and all item values have a common type shall provide an automatic type map from _{common type of the indexes} to_ _{common type of the values}.
issues.issue: "index assignment notation" is used for the glossary term "index notation".

issues.canonical: A template list with two or more items or a complemented template list, in which all templates have a common type, SHALL provide an automatic type equal to the common type.
issues.original: m) List of templates with two or more items and complemented list of templates where all templates have a common type shall provide automatic type that is equal to the common type.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether "with two or more items" also applies to the complemented list, and "and" means "or" here. Chose the reading that the minimum of two items applies only to the template list.
readings: A template list with two or more items, or a complemented template list with any number of items, SHALL provide the common type as automatic type.
A template list or a complemented template list SHALL provide the common type as automatic type only if it has two or more items.

issues.canonical: The automatic type of a value range IS equal to the type of its bounds.
issues.original: The automatic type is equal to the type of the bounds.
issues.issue: The rule does not say what happens when one bound is infinity or when the bounds have different types. Chose the reading that the type of the non-infinite bound(s) is used.
readings: The automatic type of a value range IS the type of its finite bound(s); bounds of different types are an error.
The automatic type of a value range IS the common type of both bounds, determined by the expression rules.

issues.canonical: A `superset` or `subset` matching mechanism in which all items have a common type SHALL provide the automatic type `set of` the common type.
issues.original: p) Superset and subset where all items have a common type shall provide an automatic type set of _{common_ _type}.
issues.issue: "Superset and subset" means either of the two matching mechanisms.

issues.canonical: The expression or template body used for automatic typing MAY be any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment, if its type context is unambiguous.
issues.original: The common type shall fulfil requirements for automatic typing._ q) Any other TTCN-3 language operation that can occur on the right-hand side of an assignment where the type context is unambiguous.
issues.issue: With an automatic type there is no declared type that provides a type context, so it is unclear which operations qualify; the item is open-ended. Chose the reading that the operation itself must determine its type unambiguously.
readings: Any operation whose result type is determined by the operation itself MAY be used for automatic typing.
Any operation MAY be used for automatic typing if an enclosing construct provides an unambiguous type context.

issues.canonical: A template CAN be used at the right hand side of an assignment, in parameter passing and in (predefined) functions where template passing is explicitly allowed.
issues.original: NOTE: Templates can be used at the RHS of assignment, parameter passing and (predefined) functions where template passing is explicitly allowed.
issues.issue: 'RHS' is an abbreviation of the glossary term 'right hand side (of assignment)'.

issues.canonical: An operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be a value.
issues.original: The operands of the operators used in an expression shall be values and their root types shall be the types specified for the appropriate operator in the subsequent clauses.
issues.issue: The general rule conflicts with operators such as `isvalue`, `ispresent`, `ischosen` and `isbound`, which accept template instances as operands; reading 1 (rule applies except where an operator clause states otherwise) is chosen.
readings: An operand of an operator used in an expression SHALL be a value, unless the clause of the specific operator explicitly allows templates.
An operand of any operator used in an expression SHALL be a value, without exception.

issues.canonical: An expression of a record, set, record of, set of, array, union or anytype type IS written in assignment notation or value list notation.
issues.original: Assignment or list notations are used for expressions of record, set, record of, set of, array, union and anytype types.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether both notations apply to every listed type; list notation is not allowed for union and anytype, and assignment notation is not used for record of/set of/array (which use index notation). Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: An expression of a record, set, record of, set of, array, union or anytype type IS written in the notation (assignment or value list) that is allowed for that type.
An expression of any of the types record, set, record of, set of, array, union and anytype MAY be written in either assignment notation or value list notation.

issues.canonical: The root type of an operand SHALL be one of the types specified for the operator applied to it.
issues.original: b) The root types of the operands shall be the types specified for the appropriate operand.
issues.issue: The sentence says 'types specified for the appropriate operand', where 'appropriate operator' is meant (compare 7.0-s007); it restates 7.0-007b.

issues.canonical: A predefined operator IS a member of one of the categories arithmetic, list, relational, logical, bitwise, shift, rotate or presence checking operators.
issues.original: The predefined operators fall into seven categories:
issues.issue: The sentence states 'seven categories' but the following list a) to h) has eight entries; table 5 also names the list operator category 'String operators'. The list of eight is chosen.
readings: The predefined operators fall into the eight categories listed in items a) to h).
The predefined operators fall into seven categories, one of the listed items being redundant.

issues.canonical: The concatenation operator IS denoted by the symbol or keyword `&` and belongs to the string operators (list operator) category.
issues.original: Category: String operators; Operator: concatenation; Symbol or Keyword: &
issues.issue: Table 5 places the concatenation operator `&` in category 'String operators', while clause 7.1.0 and 7.1.2 call it the 'list operator' and it also applies to record of, set of and array values.

issues.canonical: The binary `xor` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `or` operator.
issues.original: Lowest Binary **xor**
issues.issue: The PDF rendering places the label 'Lowest' at the `xor` row although `or` is listed after it; the label most likely spans the last rows, so `or` is taken as the lowest-precedence operator.
readings: The binary `xor` operator IS of higher precedence than the binary `or` operator, and `or` IS of the lowest precedence.
The binary `xor` operator IS of the lowest precedence, and `or` IS of equal or higher precedence.

issues.canonical: Dot notation, index notation and decoding notation (`=>`) SHOULD be evaluated from left to right, just after the parentheses operator and before the `ispresent`, `ischosen`, `isvalue` and `isbound` operators.
issues.original: NOTE: Dot notation ("."), index notation (" [ ] ") and the decoding notation (" => ") should be evaluated from left to right, just after the evaluation of the parentheses (" ( ) ") operator and before the evaluation of the ispresent, ischosen, isvalue, isbound operators.
issues.issue: The evaluation order is given in a NOTE with 'should', but the following normative sentence (7.1.0-s056) states it as an equivalence; it is unclear whether it is a recommendation or a binding rule. The NOTE is kept as recommendation; the binding rule is recorded as 7.1.0-056a.
readings: Dot notation, index notation and decoding notation SHOULD be evaluated from left to right, after parentheses and before the presence checking operators (recommendation).
Dot notation, index notation and decoding notation SHALL be evaluated from left to right, after parentheses and before the presence checking operators (binding rule).

issues.canonical: An operand of an arithmetic operator SHALL be an integer value (including values of types derived from integer) or a float value (including values of types derived from float) containing a numeric value only.
issues.original: Operands of these operators shall be of integer values (including derivations of integer) or floating-point numbers (including derivations of float, containing numeric values only), except for mod and rem which shall be used with integer (including derivations of integer) types only.
issues.issue: 'containing numeric values only' could exclude the special float values infinity, -infinity and not_a_number, which contradicts 7.1.1-s003; it is also not stated whether integer and float operands may be mixed. Reading 1 (special values allowed per IEEE 754, no mixing) is chosen.
readings: An operand of an arithmetic operator SHALL be an integer or float value, the special float values being allowed with IEEE 754 semantics, and both operands SHALL be of the same root type.
An operand of an arithmetic operator SHALL be an integer value or a float value that is not infinity, -infinity or not_a_number.
An arithmetic operator MAY combine an integer operand with a float operand.

issues.canonical: The result of the division operator `/` on two integer values IS the whole integer part of the quotient of the first integer by the second, with the fraction discarded.
issues.original: a) `integer values gives the whole integer part of the value resulting from dividing the first integer by` the second (i.e. fractions are discarded);
issues.issue: 'Whole integer part' does not state the rounding direction for negative quotients; truncation toward zero is chosen because it is consistent with the rem definition and table 7.
readings: Integer division truncates the quotient toward zero (e.g. -7/2 = -3).
Integer division rounds the quotient toward negative infinity (e.g. -7/2 = -4).

issues.canonical: The right operand y of the `rem` or `mod` operator SHALL NOT be zero.
issues.original: Therefore, they are only defined for non-zero operands y.
issues.issue: 'only defined for non-zero operands y' does not say whether a zero divisor is a compile-time error (for constants) or a runtime error, or whether the result is just undefined.
readings: A zero right operand of `rem` or `mod` SHALL cause an error (at compile time if known statically, otherwise at runtime).
The result of `rem` or `mod` with a zero right operand IS undefined and no error is required.

issues.canonical: The list operator `&` IS the concatenation of values of string types, record of types, set of types or arrays.
issues.original: The predefined list operator (&) performs concatenation of values of string types, record of, set of, or array of the same root types.
issues.issue: 'array of' is used for arrays; 'string types' is not a glossary term (bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring are meant).

issues.canonical: The operands of a relational operator SHALL NOT be instances of different root types.
issues.original: It is not allowed to compare instances of different root types.
issues.issue: The sentence follows the rule for <, >, >=, <= but does not say whether it also covers == and !=; for == and != the next paragraph makes an exception for enumerated types. Chosen reading: it applies to <, >, >= and <=.
readings: The operands of the relational operators <, >, >= and <= SHALL NOT be instances of different root types.
The operands of any relational operator, including == and !=, SHALL NOT be instances of different root types.

issues.canonical: If the actual type of the address type differs from the types for which equality is defined, a value of the address type SHALL only be compared with the special value `null`.
issues.original: The address type is allowed for the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators, independent of its actual type, but when its actual type differs from the types specified above, it can be compared to the literal special value null only.
issues.issue: "the types specified above" can mean the operand types of <, >, >=, <= (integer, float, enumerated) given in the previous paragraph, or the types for which equality rules are given in the list below. Chosen reading: the types for which equality rules exist.
readings: If the actual type of the address type is not one of the types for which equality is defined in clause 7.1.3, an address value SHALL only be compared with `null`.
If the actual type of the address type is not integer, float or an enumerated type, an address value SHALL only be compared with `null`.

issues.canonical: Except for enumerated types, the operands of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators SHALL be of compatible root types.
issues.original: Operands of equality (==) and non-equality (!=) shall be completely initialized values or field references, and with the exception of enumerated types, shall be of compatible root types.
issues.issue: "compatible root types" is not a defined term; clause 6.3 defines type compatibility between types, not between root types.

issues.canonical: An instance of a type for which no equality rule is given in clause 7.1.3 SHALL NOT be an operand of the equality (==) and non-equality (!=) operators.
issues.original: This implies that instances of types not mentioned below shall not be operands of equality and non-equality: The values or field references being compared shall obey the following rules.
issues.issue: The list of equality rules does not mention boolean, verdicttype, objid or address types. Taken literally, these types could not be compared with == and !=, which is surely not intended. Chosen reading: the literal one, but with an open issue for the types that are not listed.
readings: Only instances of the types listed in the equality rules of clause 7.1.3 MAY be operands of == and !=; values of boolean, verdicttype or objid types SHALL NOT be compared.
Values of basic types not listed (e.g. boolean, verdicttype) MAY be compared with == and != with obvious value equality; only types without a defined equality SHALL NOT be operands.

issues.canonical: An expression of enumerated type B SHALL only be compared with an expression of a different enumerated type A if A and B can be merged into a consistent larger enumerated type, i.e. no integer value is associated with different identifiers.
issues.original: In the case of different enumerated types, expression "b" of type "B" can be compared with expression "a" of type "A" if the two types "A" and "B" can be merged to a consistent larger enumerated type (i.e. where numbers are not associated with different identifiers, see also clause 6.3.2.1).
issues.issue: In EXAMPLE 1, EDesWeekDays and EWeekDays associate the same numbers with different identifiers and therefore cannot be merged, yet the comparison v_myDesWeekDayMon == v_myWeekDayMon is shown as returning false and not as an error. Chosen reading: the normative text (comparison is not allowed).
readings: Comparing values of two enumerated types that cannot be merged SHALL cause an error.
Values of two enumerated types that cannot be merged MAY be compared, and the comparison returns false.

issues.canonical: Two bitstring, two hexstring or two octetstring values ARE equal if and only if they have equal lengths and the bits, hexadecimal digits or octets, respectively, at all positions are the same.
issues.original: For values of bitstring, hexstring or octetstring types, the same equality rule applies as for charstring values with the exception, that fractions which shall equal at all positions are bits, hexadecimal digits or pairs of hexadecimal digits accordingly. Two charstring or two universal charstring values are equal if and only if they have equal lengths and the characters at all positions are the same.
issues.issue: "fractions" is used for the string elements, and "pairs of hexadecimal digits" for octets.

issues.canonical: Values of the same union type, and values of different union types in which at least one alternative is compatible with the other type, MAY be compared, independent of whether a compatible alternative is the selected one.
issues.original: Values of the same union type, and values of different union types in which at least one of the alternatives is compatible with the other type (see clause 6.3.2.4) can be compared (independent if a compatible alternative is the selected one or not).
issues.issue: "at least one of the alternatives is compatible with the other type" does not say whether an alternative of one union must be compatible with an alternative (with the same name) of the other union, or with the other union type as a whole. Chosen reading: per clause 6.3.2.4, an alternative with the same name and a compatible type.
readings: Values of different union types MAY be compared if at least one alternative of one union type has the same name and a compatible type as an alternative of the other union type.
Values of different union types MAY be compared if the type of at least one alternative of one union type is compatible with the other union type.

issues.canonical: Values of the same anytype, or of the anytypes of any two modules, MAY be compared.
issues.original: Values of the same or any two anytype types can be compared.
issues.issue: "any two anytype types" refers to the anytype of different modules; anytype is a single type per module.

issues.canonical: Two default, two port, two timer or two component values ARE equal if and only if both are initialized with the special value `null` or both refer to the same default, port, timer or test component, independent of the actual state of that object.
issues.original: Two default, two port, two timer or two component values are equal if and only if they both are initialized with the special value null or they both contain a reference to the same entity (i.e. they designate the same default, port, timer or test component, independent of the actual state of the denoted object).
issues.issue: "default, port, timer or component values" are references to objects; the glossary term is object reference.

issues.canonical: A compound expression (assignment notation or value list notation) MAY be used directly as an operand of a comparison operation of a structured type.
issues.original: It is also possible to use compound expressions (field assignment or value list notation) directly as operands of comparison operations of structured types.
issues.issue: "field assignment" is used for the glossary term assignment notation.

issues.canonical: Two map values ARE equal if and only if each is compatible with the type of the other operand, they have the same number of key-value pairs, and for each key-value pair in either map the other map has a key-value pair with an equal key and an equal value.
issues.original: Two maps are equal if and only if they are mutually compatible with the type of the other operand (see clause 6.3.2.2), they have the same number of key-value pairs and for each key-value pair in both maps there is a key-value pair in the other map where the key from one pair is equal to the key from the other pair and the value from one pair is equal to the value from the other pair.
issues.issue: The cross-reference to clause 6.3.2.2 (compatibility of record and set types) is used for map types.

issues.canonical: The two operands of the `and4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
issues.original: The bitwise and4b operator accepts two operands of equal length.
issues.issue: The text is a normative paragraph of the standard but was converted as example text; it is marked non-normative only because of its source unit kind. "accepts two operands of equal length" does not say whether operands of different length are an error. Chosen reading: they are an error.
readings: The operands of `and4b` SHALL have equal length; operands of different length cause an error.
The `and4b` operator is defined only for operands of equal length; the behaviour for different lengths is unspecified.

issues.canonical: The two operands of the `or4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
issues.original: The bitwise or4b operator accepts two operands of equal length.
issues.issue: The text is a normative paragraph of the standard but was converted as example text; it is marked non-normative only because of its source unit kind. "accepts two operands of equal length" does not say whether operands of different length are an error. Chosen reading: they are an error.
readings: The operands of `or4b` SHALL have equal length; operands of different length cause an error.
The `or4b` operator is defined only for operands of equal length; the behaviour for different lengths is unspecified.

issues.canonical: The two operands of the `xor4b` operator SHALL have equal length.
issues.original: The bitwise xor4b operator accepts two operands of equal length.
issues.issue: The text is a normative paragraph of the standard but was converted as example text; it is marked non-normative only because of its source unit kind. "accepts two operands of equal length" does not say whether operands of different length are an error. Chosen reading: they are an error.
readings: The operands of `xor4b` SHALL have equal length; operands of different length cause an error.
The `xor4b` operator is defined only for operands of equal length; the behaviour for different lengths is unspecified.

issues.canonical: The rotate left operator `<@` rotates the left-hand operand to the left by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
issues.original: It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the left as specified by the right-hand operand.
issues.issue: 'shift units' is used in the rotate clause, while the list above defines 'rotate unit'.

issues.canonical: For the rotate left operator `<@`, the rotate units shifted out on the left IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.
issues.original: Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.
issues.issue: 'Excess shift units' is used where 'rotate units' (as defined in the list) is meant.

issues.canonical: The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL additionally satisfy restriction a) of clause 6.5.
issues.original: NOTE 2: Note that for the right hand operand restriction a) in clause 6.5 further on applies.
issues.issue: Clause 6.5 of this version is 'Automatic type', whose item a) does not constrain operands of operators; the reference appears stale, so the intended restriction cannot be determined.
readings: The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL satisfy item a) of clause 6.5 (Automatic type).
The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL satisfy the general operator restriction a) of clause 7.1 (operands shall be initialized/of compatible type), the reference to 6.5 being outdated.

issues.canonical: The rotate right operator `@>` rotates the left-hand operand to the right by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
issues.original: It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the right as specified by the right-hand operand.
issues.issue: The rule for `@>` is placed inside the Examples block (after EXAMPLE 1) and uses 'shift units' instead of 'rotate units'.

issues.canonical: For the rotate right operator `@>`, the rotate units shifted out on the right IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its left-hand side.
issues.original: Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its left-hand side.
issues.issue: The rule is placed inside the Examples block and uses 'shift units' instead of 'rotate units'.

issues.canonical: The operand of a presence checking operator MAY be of any type.
issues.original: The operand of these operators can be of any type.
issues.issue: The general statement conflicts with 7.1.8.2, which allows `ischosen` only for union-field references and anytype alternatives. Chosen reading: any type is allowed in general, the operator-specific clauses may restrict it further.
readings: The operand of every presence checking operator MAY be of any type.
The operand of a presence checking operator MAY be of any type, unless the clause of the specific operator (e.g. 7.1.8.2 for `ischosen`) restricts the operand.

issues.canonical: Special error-handling rules apply when the operand of a presence checking operator is a data object reference, function instance, template instance or the result of a `valueof` operation followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.
issues.original: Specific rules apply if the operand of a presence checking operator is a data object reference, function instance, template instance or a result of the valueof operation followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether 'followed by an ExtendedFieldReference' qualifies only the valueof result or all listed operand forms. Chosen reading: all operand forms followed by an ExtendedFieldReference, since the following rules concern resolving the ExtendedFieldReference.
readings: The special rules apply to a data object reference, function instance, template instance or valueof result, each followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.
The special rules apply to any data object reference, function instance or template instance, and to a valueof result only when followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.

issues.canonical: The special error handling of dot notation, index notation and decoded field references in presence checking operators IS NOT applied recursively.
issues.original: The rule on special handling of dot notation, index notation and decoded field references is not applied recursively.
issues.issue: 'Not applied recursively' is not defined; the following sentence suggests it means nested expressions (index values, encoding format parameters) are not covered, but it may also mean that presence checking operators nested in the operand do not inherit the rule. Chosen reading: the rule covers only the outermost ExtendedFieldReference of the operand.
readings: Error suppression applies only to the resolution of the ExtendedFieldReference of the operand itself, not to errors inside expressions nested in it.
Error suppression is not propagated to presence checking operators or references nested inside the operand.

issues.canonical: If `ispresent` applied to a template returns `true`, that template MAY be assigned to a non-optional field of the template's type in a template variable.
issues.original: m_myTemplate can safely be assigned to a non-optional field of the type of the template in a template variable; m_myTemplate can safely be used as an actual template(present) parameter or assigned to a variable of kind template(present). NOTE 2: This means that whenever ispresent(m_myTemplate) returns true:
issues.issue: The text continues NOTE 2 (informative) but is marked as normative prose by the PDF conversion; normative=false was chosen. 'safely' expresses that no error will occur.

issues.canonical: If `ispresent` applied to a template returns `true`, that template MAY be used as an actual parameter for a `template(present)` formal parameter or assigned to a `template(present)` variable.
issues.original: m_myTemplate can safely be assigned to a non-optional field of the type of the template in a template variable; m_myTemplate can safely be used as an actual template(present) parameter or assigned to a variable of kind template(present). NOTE 2: This means that whenever ispresent(m_myTemplate) returns true:
issues.issue: The text continues NOTE 2 (informative); 'actual template(present) parameter' mixes actual and formal parameter terminology.

improper_terms.proper: actual parameter of a template(present) formal parameter

issues.canonical: The operand of the `ischosen` operator SHALL be a reference to an alternative of a union type or to a type alternative of an `anytype`.
issues.original: This operator is allowed for data objects of all data types that are a union-field-reference or a type alternative of an anytype.
issues.issue: 'is allowed for data objects of all data types that are a union-field-reference' is garbled: it is unclear whether other operands are forbidden (compile-time error) or merely meaningless; it also conflicts with 7.1.8.0 ('operand can be of any type'). Chosen reading: exclusive restriction.
readings: The operand of `ischosen` SHALL be a reference to a union alternative or anytype alternative; any other operand is an error.
The operand of `ischosen` MAY be a reference to a union alternative or anytype alternative, other operands being allowed as for all presence checking operators.

improper_terms.used: data types that are a union-field-reference
improper_terms.proper: reference to an alternative of a union type

issues.canonical: The `ischosen` operator IS applicable to data objects of union types or `anytype` that contain a specific value or a value list.
issues.original: The ischosen operator is applicable to data objects of union types or of anytype containing a specific value or a value list.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether applying `ischosen` to a union template containing another matching mechanism (e.g. `?`) is an error or yields false; EXAMPLE 1 (mw_u3 := ?) shows false. Chosen reading: other templates yield false.
readings: `ischosen` applied to a union/anytype template that is neither a specific value nor a value list yields `false`.
`ischosen` SHALL NOT be applied to a union/anytype template that is neither a specific value nor a value list (error).

issues.canonical: For the `isvalue` operator, the special value `null` IS considered a specific value.
issues.original: The specific value null is considered as concrete value.
issues.issue: 'concrete value' is used instead of 'specific value' used in the rest of the clause.

issues.canonical: For the `isbound` operator, the special value `null` IS considered a specific value.
issues.original: The specific value null is considered as concrete value.
issues.issue: 'concrete value' is used instead of 'specific value'.

issues.canonical: The decoding notation SHALL only be applied to expressions of type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring` or `universal charstring`.
issues.original: Decoded field reference is a specific notation called decoding notation that can be applied to expressions of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.
issues.issue: 'can be applied to' may be a mere capability statement or an exclusive restriction. Chosen reading: exclusive restriction, as decoding requires a string-encoded payload.
readings: The decoding notation SHALL only be applied to expressions of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.
The decoding notation CAN be applied to expressions of these string types, without excluding other types.

issues.canonical: An encoding format parameter value other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Any other value shall cause an error. The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
issues.issue: The kind of error is not specified: a compile-time error when the value is known statically, or a runtime test case error.
readings: An invalid encoding format value SHALL cause a compile-time error if statically known, otherwise a test case error.
An invalid encoding format value SHALL always cause a runtime test case error.

issues.canonical: An extended type reference following the `=>` symbol SHALL always use the extended syntax with parentheses.
issues.original: Extended type references shall always use the extended syntax with parentheses.
issues.issue: 'Extended type reference' is not defined; it presumably means any type reference other than a built-in type or single identifier (e.g. qualified names or field sub-type references).

improper_terms.proper: type reference not consisting of a single identifier

issues.canonical: The encoded form of a TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT contain characters that do not correspond to any character of the module.
issues.original: The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether a UTF-8 byte order mark counts as a 'character not corresponding to any character of the module'; the strict reading is chosen.
readings: The encoded module SHALL NOT contain any byte sequence (e.g. a byte order mark) that does not correspond to a module character.
The encoded module SHALL NOT contain invalid UTF-8 sequences; a byte order mark is tolerated.

issues.canonical: A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable.
issues.original: They are reusable and parameterizable.
issues.issue: 'Parameterizable' is not explained; given clause 8.2.1 the module-parameter reading is chosen (the module syntax has no formal parameter list).
readings: A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable by means of module parameters.
A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable with formal parameters like other parameterizable objects.

issues.canonical: A language string identifying the core language edition SHALL be one of the listed strings "TTCN-3:2001" ... "TTCN-3:2023".
issues.original: The following language strings are to be used:
issues.issue: 'are to be used' does not say whether unlisted strings are errors; the restrictive reading for the core language edition string is chosen.
readings: A language string SHALL be one of the listed strings; any other string is an error.
The listed strings are the ones to be used for core language editions; other strings (e.g. package tags) are not restricted by this list.

issues.canonical: A module complying with the present document that carries a language string SHALL use the language string "TTCN-3:2023".
issues.original:
"TTCN-3:2001" - to be used with modules complying with V1.1.2 [i.17] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2003" - to be used with modules complying with V2.2.1 [i.18] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2005" - to be used with modules complying with V3.1.1 [i.19] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2007" - to be used with modules complying with V3.2.1 [i.20] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2008" - to be used with modules complying with V3.3.2 [i.21] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2008 Amendment 1" - to be used with modules complying with V3.4.1 [i.22] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2009" - to be used with modules complying with V4.1.1 [i.23] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2010" - to be used with modules complying with V4.2.1 [i.24] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2011" - to be used with modules complying with V4.3.1 [i.25] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2012" - to be used with modules complying with V4.4.1 [i.26] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2013" - to be used with modules complying with V4.5.1 [i.27] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2014" - to be used with modules complying with V4.6.1 [i.28] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2015" - to be used with modules complying with V4.7.1 [i.29] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2016" - to be used with modules complying with V4.8.1 [i.30] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2017" - to be used with modules complying with V4.9.1 [i.31] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2018" - to be used with modules complying with V4.10.1 [i.32] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2019" - to be used with modules complying with V4.11.1 [i.33] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2020" - to be used with modules complying with V4.12.1 [i.34] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2021" - to be used with modules complying with V4.13.1 [i.35] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2022" - to be used with modules complying with V4.14.1 [i.36] of the present document.
  "TTCN-3:2023" - to be used with modules complying with the present document.
issues.issue: The present document is V4.17.1 (2025) but the list ends with "TTCN-3:2023" and has no entries for V4.15.1/V4.16.1; the literal reading is chosen.
readings: A module complying with V4.17.1 SHALL use "TTCN-3:2023".
"TTCN-3:2023" is the string for the newest edition, while V4.15.1-V4.17.1 have no own string.

issues.canonical: The language string and the package tags in the `language` attribute SHALL be written as a comma-separated list.
issues.original: The language identifier and the package identifier are to be written as a comma-separated list.
issues.issue: The sentence uses 'language identifier' and 'package identifier' for what the preceding sentences call 'language string' and 'package tag'.

issues.canonical: A module definition that is not used NEED NOT be evaluated at all.
issues.original: NOTE: If a definition is not used, it may not be evaluated at all.
issues.issue: 'may not be evaluated' can be read as a possibility or as a prohibition; the possibility reading is chosen as it fits the preceding rule.
readings: A module definition that is not used NEED NOT be evaluated.
A module definition that is not used SHALL NOT be evaluated.

issues.canonical: A declaration of a dynamic language element, such as a variable or a timer, SHALL only be made in a test case, function, altstep or component type.
issues.original: Declarations of dynamic language elements such as variables or timers shall only be made in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types.
issues.issue: The list omits the module control part, in which variables and timers are allowed (clause 26); the literal list is kept in the canonical text, the control part is considered allowed by clause 26.
readings: Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps or component types (list is exhaustive).
Variables and timers SHALL only be declared in test cases, functions, altsteps, component types and the module control part.

issues.canonical: A component variable MAY be used by all test cases, functions and altsteps running on a component of that component type.
issues.original: However, variables defined in a test component type may be used by all test cases, functions, etc. running on components of that component type.
issues.issue: Glossary term 'component variable' is meant.

improper_terms.used: variables defined in a test component type

issues.canonical: A module parameter IS a value or template that MAY be supplied by the test system at runtime.
issues.original: Module parameters are values or templates that may be supplied by the test environment at runtime.
issues.issue: The glossary term is 'test system'.

issues.canonical: Module parameterization IS restricted to value parameterization.
issues.original: For module parameterization, TTCN-3 only supports value parameterization which has to be resolved static at start of runtime.
issues.issue: 'value parameterization' conflicts with template module parameters allowed by s001/s004; the reading 'static parameterization (values and templates) resolved at start of runtime' is chosen.
readings: Module parameters are only supported as static (value) parameterization resolved at start of runtime, which includes template module parameters.
Module parameters SHALL only be values, not templates.

issues.canonical: When automatic typing is used for a module parameter, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the declaration IS omitted.
issues.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
issues.issue: The syntax block and restriction i) use 'TypeOrNestedTypeDef'.

issues.canonical: A module parameter SHALL only be of the address type if the address type is explicitly defined within the module containing the module parameter declaration.
issues.original: c) A module parameter shall only be of type address if the address type is explicitly defined within the associated module.
issues.issue: 'explicitly defined within the associated module' does not say whether an imported address type definition suffices; the literal reading is chosen.
readings: The address type SHALL be defined in the module that declares the module parameter.
The address type SHALL be defined in, or be visible (e.g. imported) in, the module associated with the module parameter.

issues.canonical: A module parameter SHALL be declared only within the module definitions part.
issues.original: d) Module parameters shall be declared within the module definition part only.
issues.issue: Clause 8.2 uses the name 'module definitions part'.

issues.canonical: Every sub-element of component or default type of the default value of a module parameter SHALL be initialized with the special value `null`.
issues.original: h) All sub-elements of component or default type of a default value of a module parameter shall be initialized with the special value null.
issues.issue: Restriction b) forbids top-level component and default types but only forbids port/timer sub-elements; the first reading is chosen.
readings: Sub-elements of component or default type in the default value SHALL be `null`.
This rule implies that module parameters of structured types with component or default sub-elements are allowed, which restriction b) does not forbid; only the default must use `null`.

issues.canonical: Top-level group identifiers of a module SHALL be unique.
issues.original: However, top-level group identifiers and all group identifiers of subgroups of a single group shall be unique.
issues.issue: It is not stated against which set of identifiers uniqueness is required; the first reading is chosen.
readings: Top-level group identifiers SHALL be unique among the top-level groups of the module.
Top-level group identifiers SHALL be unique among all top-level identifiers of the module.

issues.canonical: An import statement MAY import module parameters, user-defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and testcases.
issues.original: TTCN-3 supports the import of the following definitions: module parameters, user defined types, signatures, constants, data templates, signature templates, functions, external functions, altsteps and test cases.
issues.issue: The sentence uses "test cases" for the TTCN-3 testcase definitions and "user defined types" without hyphen.

issues.canonical: An importable definition IS composed of a name (its identifier), a specification and, for functions, altsteps and testcases, an associated behaviour description.
issues.original: Each definition has a name (defines the identifier of the definition, e.g. a function name), a specification (e.g. a type specification or a signature of a function) and in the case of functions, altsteps and test cases an associated behaviour description.
issues.issue: "test cases" is used for TTCN-3 testcase definitions.

issues.canonical: A field name used in a template definition IS a referenced definition that is referenced via the type of the template.
issues.original: NOTE 2: The referenced definitions field1, field2 and field3 of template MyTemplate are the field names of MyType5, i.e. they are referenced via MyType5.
issues.issue: The note names the template "MyTemplate" while the example defines "m_myTemplate".

issues.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported enumerated type ARE its enumerated values.
issues.original: Importable Definition: • enumerated type; Possible Local Definitions: Concrete values
issues.issue: Table 8 calls the enumerated values of an enumerated type "concrete values".

issues.canonical: The possible local definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter names.
issues.original: Importable Definition: Test case; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component types (runs on- and system clause)
issues.issue: Table 8 uses "Test case" for the TTCN-3 testcase definition.

issues.canonical: The possible referenced definitions of an imported testcase ARE its formal parameter types and the component types of its `runs on` and `system` clauses.
issues.original: Importable Definition: Test case; Possible Local Definitions: Parameter names; Possible Referenced Definitions: Parameter types, component types (runs on- and system clause)
issues.issue: Table 8 uses "Test case" for the TTCN-3 testcase definition.

issues.canonical: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (component reference is a variable, a value returned from a function, or the type is given in the `runs on`, `mtc` or `system` clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in this component type.
issues.original: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known (either when the component reference is a variable or value returned from a function or the type is defined the runs on, mtc or system clause of the calling function), the referenced port declaration shall be present in this component type.
issues.issue: The sentence is about connection operations and does not belong to the import clause; it seems to have been copied here by mistake and it separates the name-clash rule from the "one exception to this rule" that follows. Chose the literal reading as a general rule for connection operations.
readings: If the type of the component referenced in a connection operation is known, the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in this component type.
If the type of an imported component referenced in a connection operation is known, the referenced port declaration SHALL be present in that imported component type.

issues.canonical: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value that clashes with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence over that definition.
issues.original: There is one exception to this rule: when in the context of an enumerated type (see clause 6.2.4), an enumerated value is clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module, the enumerated value shall take precedence and the definition in the importing module shall be referenced by using its qualified name (see example 5 below in this clause).
issues.issue: "this rule" can refer to the directly preceding sentence (port declarations in connection operations) or to the name-clash resolution rule before it; the content shows that the name-clash rule is meant.
readings: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the rule that name clashes are resolved by prefixing the imported definition.

In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the port declaration rule for connection operations.

issues.canonical: In the context of an enumerated type, a definition of the importing module whose name clashes with an enumerated value SHALL be referenced by its qualified name.
issues.original: There is one exception to this rule: when in the context of an enumerated type (see clause 6.2.4), an enumerated value is clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module, the enumerated value shall take precedence and the definition in the importing module shall be referenced by using its qualified name (see example 5 below in this clause).
issues.issue: "this rule" can refer to the directly preceding sentence (port declarations in connection operations) or to the name-clash resolution rule before it; the content shows that the name-clash rule is meant.
readings: In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the rule that name clashes are resolved by prefixing the imported definition.

In the context of an enumerated type, an enumerated value clashing with the name of a definition in the importing module SHALL take precedence, as an exception to the port declaration rule for connection operations.

issues.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
issues.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.
issues.issue: "a function definition and alike" does not list the excluded constructs; the example also shows the control part. Chose all behaviour definitions and the control part.
readings: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function definition or any other definition outside the module definitions part (e.g. component types, groups' members are allowed).

issues.canonical: Importing an enumerated type IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
issues.original: In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
issues.issue: EXAMPLE 5 states that in module B (which imports enumerated type MyEnumType) the constant "const MyEnumType enumY" is not allowed because enumerated values restrict global names, which seems to contradict this sentence. Chose the literal text; the example may mean that the clash is only forbidden in the context of the enumerated type.
readings: Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type without restriction.

Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type, except where the definition is in the context of that enumerated type (then clause 6.2.4 applies).

issues.canonical: When a function, altstep or testcase is imported, its behaviour specification and all definitions used inside it ARE NOT visible to the importing module.
issues.original: f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.
issues.issue: "test case" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; "behaviour specification" is used where the semantic description says "behaviour description".

issues.canonical: If the source module uses language concepts that are not part of the language specification taken from the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.
issues.issue: "that language specification" most likely refers to the language specification taken from the import statement when the source module has none (previous sentence); it could also refer to any language specification of the import statement.
readings: If the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.

If the source module uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error, whether or not the source module defines a language specification.

issues.canonical: An except specification of an import statement IS NOT an exclusion of the listed definitions from being imported by other imports.
issues.original: It is important to point out, that the except statement does not exclude the definitions listed from being imported in general; all statements importing definitions of the same kind can be seen as a shorthand notation for an equivalent list of identifiers of single definitions.
issues.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

issues.canonical: An except specification excludes definitions only from the single list of definitions of the import to which it belongs.
issues.original: The except statement excludes definitions from this single list only.
