issues.issue: 'except statement' is used for the except specification, which is not a statement.

issues.canonical: The `all` keyword used with the `const` keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the module definitions part of the module referenced by the import statement.
issues.original: The all keyword used with the constant keyword identifies all visible constants declared in the definitions part of the module the import statement refers to.
issues.issue: 'constant keyword' is used, the TTCN-3 keyword is `const`.

issues.canonical: The except specification of an import of all definitions SHALL contain at most one except entry per kind of definition (group, type, etc.).
issues.original: b) In the set of except statements for an all import, only one except statement per kind of definition (i.e. for a group, type, etc.) is allowed.
issues.issue: 'except statement' is used for the per-kind entries of the except specification.

issues.canonical: A language specification MAY additionally use the package identifiers defined in ETSI ES 202 781, ETSI ES 202 782, ETSI ES 202 784 and ETSI ES 202 785.
issues.original: Package identifiers from ETSI ES 202 781 [i.11], ETSI ES 202 782 [i.14], ETSI ES 202 784 [i.12] and ETSI ES 202 785 [i.13] can be used in addition.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether package identifiers may be used instead of or only together with a TTCN-3 language identifier.
readings: A language specification MAY contain package identifiers in addition to a TTCN-3 language identifier.
A language specification MAY consist of package identifiers as an alternative to TTCN-3 language identifiers.

issues.canonical: When an incompatibility is discovered between the language or package identification (including implicit identification by omitting the language specification) and the syntax of the module from which definitions are imported, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL make a reasonable effort to resolve the conflict.
issues.original: When an incompatibility is discovered between the language and/or package identification (including implicit identification by omitting the language specification) and the syntax of the module from which definitions are imported, tools shall provide reasonable effort to resolve the conflict.
issues.issue: 'Reasonable effort' is not defined; it is unclear whether the tool must still report an error if resolution fails.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL attempt to resolve the conflict and MAY report an error if the attempt fails.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL resolve the conflict and SHALL NOT report an error.

issues.canonical: When a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of the fields of that type SHALL be accessible and are used for the template definition.
issues.original: For example, when a template is defined based on a structured type, the identifiers and types of fields of the core type shall be accessible and are used for the template definition.
issues.issue: 'core type' is used for the type on which the template is based; the glossary defines core type as the type directly referencing the root type.

issues.canonical: A versioned or foreign element used as the type of a TTCN-3 definition SHALL provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.
issues.original: In a similar way, when a core type is a versioned or foreign element it shall provide the same information content as would be required from a TTCN-3 type declaration.
issues.issue: 'core type' is used for the referenced type of a definition rather than in the glossary sense.

issues.canonical: The language specification of an import statement SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and its TTCN-3 version is known.
issues.original: a) The language specification should only be omitted if the referenced module contains TTCN-3 notation and the TTCN-3 version is known.
issues.issue: 'the TTCN-3 version is known' does not say by whom or how it is known.
readings: The language specification SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module is TTCN-3 and its edition is known to the tool (e.g. by its own language specification).
The language specification SHOULD be omitted only if the referenced module is TTCN-3 of the same edition as the importing module.

issues.canonical: The rules for importing definitions from specifications written in other languages, e.g. SDL packages, MAY follow the TTCN-3 rules or MAY be defined separately.
issues.original: The rules for importing definitions from specifications written in other languages, e.g. SDL packages, may follow the TTCN-3 rules or may have to be defined separately.
issues.issue: 'may' could express a possibility for language mapping authors or a permission for tools.
readings: Language mapping specifications CAN define import rules that follow the TTCN-3 rules or define their own rules.
A TTCN-3 tool MAY apply its own import rules for definitions from other languages.

issues.canonical: The TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement SHALL be lower than or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
issues.original: c) A TTCN-3 module shall only import from earlier or same editions of TTCN-3 but not from later editions, e.g. the TTCN-3 language specification in an import statement has to be lower or equal to the TTCN-3 language specification of the importing module.
issues.issue: The rule is introduced with 'e.g.' although it restates the edition rule ('i.e.' seems meant); also the ordering of language identifiers is not explicitly defined.
readings: The import statement's TTCN-3 language specification SHALL denote an edition not later than the importing module's edition (comparison by edition date).
The comparison of language specifications is only one example; other checks of edition ordering may apply instead.

issues.canonical: A friend module declaration that references a missing module SHALL NOT cause an error.
issues.original: Missing friend modules shall not cause an error.
issues.issue: 'Missing' is not defined: it may mean a module that does not exist at all or one that is not part of the current compilation.
readings: A friend module declaration naming a module that does not exist in the test suite SHALL NOT cause an error.
A friend module declaration naming a module that is not available to the tool in the current build SHALL NOT cause an error.

issues.canonical: A friend module declaration SHALL have only `private` visibility, if any visibility is specified.
issues.original: a) Only private visibility can be defined for friend definitions as they are always private.
issues.issue: 'friend definitions' is used for friend module declarations.

issues.canonical: A top-level module definition without an explicit visibility modifier IS public by default, except for imported definitions and friend definitions.
issues.original: They are by default public except for imported and friend definitions.
issues.issue: 'friend definitions' (definitions with explicit friend visibility) cannot be default-public, since their visibility is explicit; the exception is redundant and the term is not defined.

issues.canonical: An import statement without an explicit visibility modifier IS private by default.
issues.original: Import definitions are by default private.
issues.issue: 'Import definitions' is used for import statements; elsewhere 'import statement' and 'imported definition' are used.

issues.canonical: A friend definition IS private only.
issues.original: Friend definitions are private only.
issues.issue: Chosen reading: 'friend definitions' denotes friend module declarations (clause 8.2.4), which can only be private. The term is undefined and could be confused with definitions having friend visibility.
readings: A friend module declaration (friend module X) SHALL only have private visibility.
A definition with friend visibility IS not importable by non-friend modules (i.e. private towards them).

issues.canonical: A group definition IS public only.
issues.original: Group definitions are public only.
issues.issue: 'Group definitions' vs 'groups' in 8.2.5-s014; same meaning.

issues.canonical: The visibility of an imported definition IS private by default.
issues.original: The visibility of imported definitions is by default private.
issues.issue: Visibility applies to import statements (s003, table 10); chosen reading: the imported definitions are by default not re-importable from the importing module, as the import statement is private.
readings: An import statement without visibility modifier is private, so the definitions imported by it are not re-exported.
An imported definition itself carries a private visibility in the importing module.

issues.canonical: Membership of a top-level definition or an import statement in a group IS NOT affecting the importability of that definition.
issues.original: If the top-level definition or the import statement is part of a group, this has no effect on the importability of the module definition.
issues.issue: Chosen reading: the visibility of the definition alone determines importability, including via group import (consistent with table 9).
readings: Group membership never changes the visibility/importability of the definition (a private definition in a group is not imported by group import).
Group membership has no effect on direct import, but importability via group import is still governed separately.

issues.canonical: A TTCN-3 module CAN contain at most one module control part.
issues.original: NOTE: As the control part is a short hand notation of a control function with the name "control", at most 1 control part can be defined in a TTCN-3 module.
issues.issue: The note derives the limit from the name clash; chosen the plain reading (at most one control part). Whether a control part plus an explicit control function is also forbidden is implied but not stated.
readings: A module SHALL NOT contain more than one control part.
A module SHALL NOT contain both a control part and an explicitly declared function named control, nor more than one control part.

issues.canonical: If the referenced module control function has no parameters, the parameter list MAY be omitted at the place of invocation.
issues.original: If the referenced module control function does not have any parameters, the parameter list may also be omitted at the place of invocation.
issues.issue: 'parameter list' at the invocation means the actual parameter list (the parentheses).

issues.canonical: A component type (keyword `component`) SHALL be defined in the module definitions part.
issues.original: Test component types and port types, denoted by the keywords component and port, shall be defined in the module definitions part.
issues.issue: 'Test component types' is used where the standard elsewhere says 'component type'.

issues.canonical: A port queue IS storing the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the test component owning that port.
issues.original: Each port is modelled as an infinite FIFO queue which stores the incoming messages or procedure calls until they are processed by the component owning that port (see figure 5).
issues.issue: 'procedure calls' may be meant literally or as shorthand for all procedure-based communication (calls, replies, exceptions); the broader reading was chosen.
readings: A port queue IS storing incoming messages and all procedure-based items (calls, replies and exceptions) until they are processed by the owning test component.
A port queue IS storing only incoming messages and procedure calls until they are processed by the owning test component.

issues.canonical: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
issues.original: A port owned by a component A shall not be connected with two or more ports owned by the same component (figure 7 (a) and (e)).
issues.issue: 'the same component' can refer to component A itself or to any single component; since item 9.1-s015 separately covers ports of a different component B, the reading 'component A itself' was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by component A itself.
A port owned by a test component A SHALL NOT be connected with two or more ports owned by any single test component (A or another one).

issues.canonical: A port owned by a test component SHALL have at most a one-to-one connection with the test system interface, i.e. it SHALL NOT be connected to more than one port of the test system interface.
issues.original: A port owned by a component A can only have a one-to-one connection with the test system interface. This means, connections as shown in figure 7 (d) are not allowed.
issues.issue: 'one-to-one' could restrict only the component port side or also the test system interface port side; since one-to-many connections are allowed (figure 6) and 9.1-s014 only restricts ports of the same component, the component-side reading was chosen.
readings: A port owned by a test component SHALL NOT be mapped to more than one port of the test system interface.
A port owned by a test component and the test system interface port it is mapped to SHALL both have no other mapping.

issues.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check the restrictions on connections at runtime.
issues.original: The checks shall be made at runtime and shall lead to a test case error when failing.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether all connection checks or only those that cannot be performed at compile-time shall be made at runtime; the latter reading was chosen as most likely, but the canonical is phrased generally.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check at runtime those connection restrictions that cannot be checked at compile-time.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL check all connection restrictions at runtime, regardless of compile-time checks.

issues.canonical: A well-defined abstract test system interface SHALL be associated with each test case.
issues.original: Instead, a well defined (but abstract) test system interface shall be associated with each test case.
issues.issue: This conflicts on its face with 9.2-s023 (test system interface need not be associated when only the MTC is used); the reading that the association may be implicit was chosen.
readings: Each test case SHALL have a test system interface, either explicitly given (system clause) or implicitly defined by the MTC component type.
Each test case SHALL explicitly declare a test system interface.

issues.canonical: A test system interface definition IS identical to a component type definition.
issues.original: A test system interface definition is identical to a component definition, i.e. it is a list of all possible communication ports through which the test case is connected to the SUT.
issues.issue: 'component definition' is used where 'component type definition' is meant.

issues.canonical: When a component type is used as a test system interface, the test system interface CANNOT make use of the constants, variables and timers declared in that component type.
issues.original: When used as test system interfaces, components cannot make use of any constants, variables and timers declared in the component type.
issues.issue: 'cannot make use' can be a rule (referencing such declarations via the system component is an error) or a statement of fact (they are not available / have no effect, cf. 9.2-s025); the factual reading was chosen.
readings: The constants, variables and timers declared in a component type used as test system interface ARE not usable by the test system interface (no effect).
A reference to a constant, variable or timer of a component type used as test system interface SHALL be rejected as an error.

issues.canonical: A test case using more than one test component SHALL be associated with a component type reference defining the test system interface.
issues.original: Generally, a component type reference defining the test system interface shall be associated with every test case using more than one test component.
issues.issue: 'Generally' weakens the SHALL; it is unclear whether it is a strict rule or a general guideline with exceptions.
readings: A test case using more than one test component SHALL have a `system` clause referencing a component type.
A test case using more than one test component SHOULD normally have a `system` clause; omitting it is not an error.

issues.canonical: The `system` operation SHALL be used to address the ports of the test system interface.
issues.original: This shall be used to address the ports of the test system.
issues.issue: 'ports of the test system' is used where 'ports of the test system interface' is meant.

issues.canonical: A variable, timer or constant declared in a component type that is used as test system interface IS without effect.
issues.original: Variables, timers and constants declared in component types, which are used as test system interfaces will have no effect.
issues.issue: 'will have no effect' is informal; the plural 'component types' is meant as a component type used as test system interface.

improper_terms.used: Variables, timers and constants declared in component types
improper_terms.proper: component variables, component timers and component constants

issues.canonical: A constant SHALL be defined only once in a TTCN-3 module.
issues.original: The constant is defined only once, but can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
issues.issue: "defined only once" can be read as a uniqueness-of-identifier rule or as describing single definition; the first (uniqueness within scope, cf. clause 5) is chosen as the testable reading.
readings: A constant identifier SHALL be declared only once within its scope.
Each constant SHALL have exactly one definition (no separate declaration and definition) in a TTCN-3 module.

issues.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of the constant declaration IS missing.
issues.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part is missing and the type is equal to the type of the expression on the right-hand side of the assignment.
issues.issue: The syntax block uses TypeOrNestedTypeDef; TypeOrNestedParDef is not part of the constant declaration syntax.

issues.canonical: An optional field of a record or set constant or of a constant field MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
issues.original: Optional fields of record and set constants or constant fields can be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
issues.issue: "constant fields" is not defined; read as fields (of record/set type) nested inside a constant. The first reading is chosen.
readings: An optional field of a record or set constant, or an optional field of a record or set field of a constant, MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.
An optional field of a record or set constant, or an optional field of a field of a constant of any structured type, MAY be initialized explicitly or implicitly.

issues.canonical: Referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` using dot notation or index notation SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: c) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.3.0) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The restriction is located in the constants clause but is not limited to constants in its wording; also unclear whether the error is a compile-time or runtime error. The general reading (any address value) is used in canonical.
readings: Referencing a field, alternative or element of a constant of address type whose actual value is `null` using dot or index notation SHALL cause an error.
Referencing a field, alternative or element of any address value (constant, variable or parameter) whose actual value is `null` using dot or index notation SHALL cause an error.

issues.canonical: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part of a variable declaration IS absent.
issues.original: When automatic typing is used, the TypeOrNestedParDef part of the declaration is missing and the type of the variable is equal to the type of the expression or template body on the right-hand side of the assignment.
issues.issue: The sentence names the syntax element TypeOrNestedParDef, but the variable declaration syntax in clauses 11.1 and 11.2 uses TypeOrNestedTypeDef.

issues.canonical: A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions running on that component type.
issues.original: These variables can be used in test cases, altsteps and functions which are running on a given component type.
issues.issue: 'running on a given component type' does not state whether compatible component types (clause 6.3.3) are included; the first reading is chosen as the literal one.
readings: A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions whose runs on clause references that component type.
A variable declared in a component type definition MAY be used in testcases, altsteps and functions whose runs on clause references that component type or a component type compatible with it.

issues.canonical: Use of an uninitialized value variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: d) Use of uninitialized value variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; the canonical text keeps the generic 'error'. Also unclear whether passing to an in formal parameter is excluded from the error.
readings: Use of an uninitialized value variable in any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement or an actual parameter SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized value variable in any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement or an actual parameter SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.

issues.canonical: The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable MAY contain a direct or indirect reference to that variable.
issues.original: g) The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable might contain a direct or indirect reference to this variable.
issues.issue: 'might' is unclear between a permission and a possibility; read together with the next sentence the self-reference is statically allowed but leads to a dynamic error on evaluation. The permission reading is chosen.
readings: The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable MAY (is permitted to) contain a direct or indirect reference to that variable.
The expression assigned to a lazy or fuzzy variable CAN (possibly) contain a direct or indirect reference to that variable, which is a situation to be handled by the following rule.

issues.canonical: A template variable declaration IS the `var template` keywords followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
issues.original: They are declared by the `var template` keyword followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
issues.issue: The prose speaks of a single 'var template keyword' and only a type identifier, while the syntactical structure uses `var` TemplateModifier (template, possibly with restriction) and TypeOrNestedTypeDef (which also allows a nested type definition or automatic typing).

improper_terms.proper: `var` keyword followed by a template modifier (TemplateModifier)

issues.canonical: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable.
issues.original: An initial content can be assigned at declaration.
issues.issue: The prose suggests an optional initial content, but the syntax block of 11.2 makes ":=" TemplateBody mandatory. The prose reading is kept in the canonical text; test authors should follow the syntax block.
readings: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable (the assignment is optional).
A template variable declaration SHALL assign an initial content, as the syntactical structure requires ":=" TemplateBody.

issues.canonical: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.
issues.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.
issues.issue: 'the variable on the left hand side' does not say whether a field or element of a template variable counts; the second reading is consistent with 11.2-s006, the first is the literal reading and is chosen.
readings: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.

If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the target on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable or a field of a template variable (e.g. accessed via dot or index notation).

issues.canonical: The dot notation and the index notation MAY be used to inspect and modify fields of a template variable, although TTCN-3 operations SHALL NOT be applied directly to template variables.
issues.original: NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.
issues.issue: The NOTE says 'TTCN-3 operations' while restriction b) it explains speaks of 'TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1)'.

issues.canonical: Use of an uninitialized template variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; since template variable declarations require an initial TemplateBody, it is also unclear how a template variable can be uninitialized. The generic reading is chosen.
readings: Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.

issues.canonical: A template variable SHALL be completely initialized in order to be used in a sending or receiving operation, as global and local templates.
issues.original: g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.
issues.issue: 'fully specified' is not a defined term; the glossary term 'completely initialized' is meant. For sending operations the template additionally has to resolve to a value (clause 15.0).

issues.canonical: A timer declared in a component type definition MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep that runs on that component type.
issues.original: These timers can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps which are running on the given component type.
issues.issue: 'running on the given component type' does not say whether compatible (extended) component types are included; chose the literal reading.
readings: A component timer MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep whose runs on clause references the component type.
A component timer MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep whose runs on clause references the component type or a type compatible with it (e.g. an extending component type).

issues.canonical: A timer value SHALL be a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
issues.original: The timer value shall be a non-negative float value (i.e. greater than or equal to 0.0) where the base unit is seconds.
issues.issue: 'The timer value' follows the default duration sentences; chose the general reading that covers all timer values.
readings: A default duration value in a timer declaration SHALL be a non-negative float value.
Any timer value (default duration or value given in a start operation) SHALL be a non-negative float value.

issues.canonical: A timer declaration has the syntax `timer` followed by one or more TimerIdentifier [ArrayDef] ":=" TimerValue items separated by optional commas, optionally terminated by ";".
issues.original: timer { TimerIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TimerValue [ "," ] } [ ";" ]
issues.issue: The syntactical structure shows the default value assignment as mandatory, contradicting the prose and example; the optional reading is the intended one.
readings: The ":=" TimerValue part of a timer declaration IS mandatory, as written in the syntactical structure.
The ":=" TimerValue part of a timer declaration IS optional, as stated in the prose (s005) and shown in EXAMPLE 1 (t_myTimer2).

issues.canonical: A timer declared and started in a scope unit (e.g. a function) ceases to exist when the scope unit is left, unless a constant, variable or parameter of the current or a higher scope unit or of an activated altstep contains a reference to the timer.
issues.original: A timer declared and started in scope units such as functions ceases to exist when the scope unit is left unless there is a constant, variable or parameter defined in the current or higher scope unit or in an activated altstep that contains a reference to it.
issues.issue: 'parameter' is used where a formal parameter holding a timer reference is meant.

issues.canonical: The default duration value of a timer array SHALL resolve to an array of non-negative numerical `float` values (not `infinity` or `not_a_number`).
issues.original: b) In case of a timer array, it shall resolve to an array of float values obeying to restriction a) above of the same size as the size of the timer array.
issues.issue: Restriction b) does not mention elements skipped with "-" (allowed by s011); chose the reading that excludes skipped elements implicitly.
readings: Every element of the default duration array of a timer array SHALL be a non-negative numerical float value.
Every element of the default duration array that is not the not used symbol SHALL be a non-negative numerical float value.

issues.canonical: Any type MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.
issues.original: Any type can be declared as type of a message in a message port type definition, i.e. values of any basic or structured type (see clauses 6.1 and 6.2) can be sent or received.
issues.issue: "Any type" is narrowed by the "i.e." clause to basic and structured types; it is unclear whether non-data types (e.g. port, component, default or timer types) may also be message types. The canonical text keeps the literal wording.
readings: Any type, including non-data types, MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.
Any data type (a basic type or a structured type) MAY be declared as the type of a message in a message port type definition.

issues.canonical: A template used to receive a message MAY be declared as a combination of values and matching mechanisms.
issues.original: Received messages can also be declared as a combination of value and matching mechanisms (see clause 15.5).
issues.issue: A received message is a value; what is declared as a combination of values and matching mechanisms is the template used in the receiving operation.

issues.canonical: A message MAY be passed via a value formal parameter or a template formal parameter.
issues.original: Instances of messages can be declared by global, local or in-line templates (see clause 15.0) or being constructed and passed via variables or template variables (see clause 11) and parameters or template parameters (see clause 5.4).
issues.issue: "parameters or template parameters" refers to value and template formal parameters (see clause 5.4).

issues.canonical: A procedure signature SHALL be defined in the TTCN-3 module for every procedure used for procedure-based communication among test components, called from the SUT or called from the test system.
issues.original: For all used procedures, i.e. procedures used for the communication among test components, procedures called from the SUT and procedures called from the test system, a procedure signature shall be defined in the TTCN-3 module.
issues.issue: "the TTCN-3 module" does not say which module; signatures may be imported (clause 8.2.3), so the most likely reading is that the signature is defined in some TTCN-3 module visible to the user, not necessarily the using module.
readings: A procedure signature SHALL be defined in some TTCN-3 module (possibly imported) for every used procedure.
A procedure signature SHALL be defined in the same TTCN-3 module in which the procedure is used.

issues.canonical: The parameter list of a signature definition MAY include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction (`in`, `out` or `inout`).
issues.original: Within a signature definition the parameter list may include parameter identifiers, parameter types and their direction, i.e. in, out, or inout.
issues.issue: "may include" suggests all three items are optional, but the syntax (14-s004) makes the type and identifier mandatory for each parameter and only the direction optional. The canonical text keeps the literal reading; the syntax reading is the likely intent.
readings: Each signature parameter SHALL have a type and an identifier, and MAY have a direction (`in`, `out` or `inout`).
A signature parameter MAY omit its identifier, type or direction.

issues.canonical: A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check an exception raised by a remote procedure.
issues.original: Therefore templates and matching mechanisms can be used to specify or check return values of remote procedures.
issues.issue: The sentence starts with "Therefore" after a sentence about exceptions but speaks of "return values"; most likely "exceptions" (values of exception types) is meant. Both readings are true in the language.
readings: A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check an exception raised by a remote procedure.
A template or a matching mechanism MAY be used to specify or check the return value of a remote procedure.

issues.canonical: A template MAY specify values, ranges and matching attributes, which MAY then be used in both message-based and procedure-based communication.
issues.original: Within a template values, ranges and matching attributes can be specified and then used in both message-based and procedure-based communications.
issues.issue: 'matching attributes' is used instead of the standard term 'matching mechanisms'.

issues.canonical: A template MAY be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.
issues.original: Templates may be specified for any TTCN-3 type or procedure signature.
issues.issue: Restriction a) of the same clause limits templates to component data types and signatures, so 'any TTCN-3 type' conflicts with it. Reading 2 is chosen, because the restriction is more specific.
readings: A template MAY be specified for every TTCN-3 type without exception, and for any procedure signature.
A template MAY be specified for any TTCN-3 type that is a component data type, and for any procedure signature.

issues.canonical: A type-based (message) template IS used for message-based communication.
issues.original: The type-based templates are used for message-based communications and the signature templates are used in procedure-based communications.
issues.issue: 'type-based templates' is used for what clause 15.1 and 15.3 call 'message templates'.

issues.canonical: The fuzzy feature of a fuzzy template IS valid only in the scope where the name of the template is visible.
issues.original: f) Fuzzy features are valid only in the scope, where the templates' names are visible.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether 'the templates' names' means the name of the template declaration only, or also the names of formal parameters to which the template is passed (the following sentence implies that a fuzzy formal parameter keeps the feature). Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The fuzzy feature IS valid only where the fuzzy template is referenced by its own name or through a formal template parameter declared `@fuzzy`.
The fuzzy feature IS valid only in the scope of the template declaration, and never inside a called function.

issues.canonical: A template used for receiving MAY contain the matching mechanisms defined in clauses 15.6.6, 15.8 and annex B.
issues.original: Matching mechanisms, as defined in clauses 15.6.6 and 15.8 and in annex B, may be used in receive templates.
issues.issue: 'receive templates' is used for templates used in receiving operations (receive, trigger, check).

issues.canonical: A signature template used in a `call` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `in` and `inout` parameters, and a signature template used in a `reply` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `out` and `inout` parameters.
issues.original: A template used in a call or reply operation defines a complete set of field values for all in and inout parameters.
issues.issue: The text says 'all in and inout parameters' also for the reply operation, but restriction a) of the same clause requires out/inout parameters to resolve in a reply. Reading 2 is chosen, consistent with restriction a).
readings: A signature template used in a `call` or `reply` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `in` and `inout` parameters.
A signature template used in a `call` operation IS the complete set of field values for all `in` and `inout` parameters, and in a `reply` operation for all `out` and `inout` parameters.

issues.canonical: In a signature template used in a `call` operation, the template specification for an `out` parameter IS ignored.
issues.original: Any template specification for out parameters is simply ignored, therefore it is allowed to specify matching mechanisms for these fields, or to omit them (see annex B).
issues.issue: The sentence follows the call-operation sentence but does not state the operation explicitly; it could also apply to every outgoing use (call, raise). Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: In a signature template used in a `call` operation, the template specification for an `out` parameter IS ignored.
In any signature template used in any operation, the template specification for an `out` parameter IS ignored.

issues.canonical: A function used for the initialization of a template SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
issues.original: If functions are used for the initialization of module parameters, it is strongly advised to adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
issues.issue: The sentence says 'module parameters' in the template clause; it most likely means functions used for initializing templates. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: A function used for the initialization of a template SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.
A function used for the initialization of a module parameter SHOULD adhere to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.

issues.canonical: The "->" symbol SHALL be used to retrieve values from templates in communication events.
issues.original: The "->" symbol shall be used for this purpose (see clause 23).
issues.issue: 'for this purpose' refers to both setting and retrieving values; the '->' symbol only redirects (retrieves) received values. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The "->" symbol SHALL be used to retrieve values from received messages in communication events.
The "->" symbol SHALL be used both to set and to retrieve values in templates in communication events.

issues.canonical: After completing initialization, a global or local message template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL be completely initialized.
issues.original: d) After completing initialization, global and local message templates that do not contain the @abstract modifier shall be fully initialized.
issues.issue: 'fully initialized' is used instead of the glossary term 'completely initialized'.

issues.canonical: After completing initialization, a global or local signature template without the `@abstract` modifier SHALL fulfil at least one of the following: all procedure parameters are completely initialized; or all `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol; or all `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol.
issues.original: e) After completing initialization, global and local signature templates that do not contain the @abstract modifier shall fulfil at least one of the following conditions: All procedure parameters are fully initialized. All in and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all out procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol. All out and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all in procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
issues.issue: 'fully initialized' is used instead of 'completely initialized', and 'unitialized' is a misspelling of 'uninitialized'.

issues.canonical: A signature template whose procedure parameters are all completely initialized IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
issues.original: All procedure parameters are fully initialized.
issues.issue: 'fully initialized' is used instead of 'completely initialized'.

issues.canonical: A signature template in which all `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
issues.original: All in and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all out procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
issues.issue: 'unitialized' is a misspelling of 'uninitialized'.

issues.canonical: A signature template whose `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `out` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol SHALL NOT be used in `reply` and `getreply` operations.
issues.original: Templates declared this way are safe to be used in call and getcall operations, but they shall not be used in reply and getreply operations. All in and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all out procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether the prohibition applies only to templates that satisfy this condition and not the 'all parameters fully initialized' condition, or to any template having this shape. Reading 1 is chosen, since a template with all parameters initialized also satisfies this condition but is not meant to be prohibited.
readings: A signature template that has uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol `out` parameters SHALL NOT be used in `reply` and `getreply` operations.
Any signature template whose `in` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized SHALL NOT be used in `reply` and `getreply` operations.

issues.canonical: A signature template in which all `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and all `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol IS a valid non-abstract signature template.
issues.original: All out and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all in procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
issues.issue: 'unitialized' is a misspelling of 'uninitialized'.

issues.canonical: A signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized and whose `in` parameters are uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.
issues.original: Templates declared this way are safe to be used in reply and getreply operations, but they shall not be used in call and getcall operations. All out and inout procedure parameters are completely initialized and all in procedure parameters are either unitialized or marked as not relevant using the NotUsedSymbol.
issues.issue: Same issue as for the call/getcall variant: unclear whether a template with all parameters completely initialized is also affected. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: A signature template that has uninitialized or NotUsedSymbol `in` parameters SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.
Any signature template whose `out` and `inout` parameters are completely initialized SHALL NOT be used in `call` and `getcall` operations.

issues.canonical: An in-line template IS an argument of a communication operation or an actual parameter of a testcase, function or altstep call, and is therefore always placed within parentheses and potentially separated by a comma.
issues.original: NOTE 1: An in-line template is an argument of a communication operation or an actual parameter of a testcase, function or altstep call, i.e. it is always placed within parenthesis and potentially separated with a comma.
issues.issue: The NOTE claims in-line templates are 'always' arguments in parentheses, but restriction c) of the same clause allows them on the right hand side of assignments and in return statements; the second reading is consistent with the normative text.
readings: An in-line template IS only ever used as an argument of a communication operation or as an actual parameter of a testcase, function or altstep call.
An in-line template IS typically used as such an argument, but may also appear in other places (e.g. right hand side of assignments, return statements, match operations) as allowed by restriction c).

issues.canonical: The type of an in-line template SHOULD only be omitted when the type is implicitly unambiguous.
issues.original: b) The type field should only be omitted when the type is implicitly unambiguous.
issues.issue: Restriction item uses 'should', yet an ambiguous type cannot be resolved by a tool, so it effectively acts as a SHALL; 'type field' is also non-standard wording for the optional Type prefix. The recommendation reading is kept as literally stated.
readings: The type of an in-line template SHOULD only be omitted when the type is implicitly unambiguous (a style recommendation; omission in ambiguous cases is still legal).
The type of an in-line template SHALL only be omitted when the type is implicitly unambiguous (omitting it in ambiguous cases is an error).

improper_terms.proper: type (Type ":" prefix of the in-line template)

issues.canonical: The type of a constant, parameter or variable of the actual scope IS always unambiguous and therefore MAY always be omitted in an in-line template.
issues.original: NOTE 3: Types of constants, parameters and variables of the actual scope are always unambiguous and can hence always be omitted.
issues.issue: 'parameters' means formal parameters visible in the scope; 'actual scope' is a non-standard term for the current scope.

issues.canonical: An in-line template containing matching mechanisms instead of or inside values SHALL only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (`receive`, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`), in arguments of the `match` operation and `select case` statement, in actual template parameters, on the right hand side of assignments to template variables, and in return statements of template returning functions.
issues.original: c) In-line templates containing instead of values or inside values matching mechanisms (see clause 15.7) can only be defined in arguments of receiving communication operations (i.e. receive, `trigger`, `check`, `getcall`, `getreply` and `catch`), in arguments of the match and select case operations, in actual template parameters, at the right hand side of assignments (when there is a template variable at the left hand side of the assignment) and in return statements of template returning functions.
issues.issue: 'select case' is a statement, not an operation; 'can only be defined' is read as a restriction (SHALL only).

issues.canonical: When an in-line template is used in a communication operation, the type of the in-line template SHALL be in the list of types of the port over which the template is sent or received.
issues.original: d) When used in communication operations, the type of the in-line template shall be in the port list over which the template is sent or received.
issues.issue: 'port list' means the list of message types/signatures of the port type definition.

improper_terms.proper: message or signature list of the port type

issues.canonical: For templates, template fields and list elements of simple types, union types and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template replaces the corresponding content of the parent template.
issues.original: a) In case of templates, template fields or list elements of simple types, union and enumerated types, the matching mechanism specified in the modified template is simply replacing its corresponding content in its parent.
issues.issue: 'simple types' is not a defined term; 'basic types' is the glossary term.

issues.canonical: The index assignment notation in a modified template SHALL only be used when individual elements of a record of or set of template or template field are to be changed.
issues.original: when individual values of a modified template or a modified template field of record of or set of type wished to be changed, and only in these cases, the index assignment notation may also be used, where the left hand side of the assignment is the index of the element to be altered.
issues.issue: 'and only in these cases' may restrict usage to record of/set of types or may refer to modifying individual elements; read as a restriction to record of/set of.
readings: Index assignment notation SHALL only be used for record of / set of templates or fields in a modified template.
Index assignment notation in a modified template MAY be used for record of / set of; 'only in these cases' merely restates that it changes individual elements and does not prohibit other uses.

issues.canonical: For record of and set of types, rule (c) (e.g. truncation) IS applied first to the complete structure, and the further modification rules are then applied to the remaining individual elements.
issues.original: In case of record of and set of types first apply rule (c) to the complete structure (e.g. truncation) than apply further rules for the remaining individual type structure elements (see example 3).
issues.issue: Typo 'than' for 'then'; 'type structure elements' means the remaining elements of the record of / set of value.

issues.canonical: If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template derived from it SHALL have the same or a less strict template restriction (see table 13b).
issues.original: f) If the base template has a restriction, the modified template derived from it shall have the same or less strict template restriction (see table 13b in clause 15.8).
issues.issue: The example 8 comments ('Allowed ... less restrictive') match the first reading, but deriving a less strict template from a restricted one contradicts the usual parameter rule in item b)2) ('stricter'); first reading chosen per the text and example.
readings: If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template SHALL have the same or a less strict template restriction (an unrestricted modified template is allowed).
If the base template has a template restriction, the modified template SHALL have the same or a stricter template restriction.

issues.canonical: An individual string element of a template of a character string type MAY be referenced if the template contains a specific value, a pattern or AnyValue, or, when the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment, AnyValueOrNone.
issues.original: The template is of a character string type and it contains either a specific value, pattern or AnyValue or when occurring on the left hand AnyValueOrNone.
issues.issue: The phrase 'when occurring on the left hand AnyValueOrNone' is garbled; it was read as 'AnyValueOrNone when the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment'.
readings: An individual string element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone MAY be referenced only when the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment.
An individual string element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone MAY be referenced on either side of an assignment.

issues.canonical: A template whose individual string elements are referenced MAY contain the ifpresent and length matching attributes.
issues.original: In any of the cases mentioned above, the reference template might contain ifpresent and length matching attributes.
issues.issue: 'reference template' is used where 'referenced template' is meant.

issues.canonical: When the referenced template is of a character string type to which a pattern is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of characters and indexable metacharacters in the pattern, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing the single referenced character or metacharacter.
issues.original: b) A pattern containing either a single character or a single metacharacter, if the referenced template is of a character sting type to which a pattern is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of characters and indexable metacharacters inside the pattern.
issues.issue: Typo 'character sting type' for 'character string type'.

issues.canonical: When the referenced template is of a character string type and contains AnyValueOrNone, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing a single ? metacharacter with the ifpresent matching attribute attached.
issues.original: f) A pattern containing a single ? metacharacter with the ifpresent matching attribute attached to it if the referenced template is of a character string type and contains the AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism.
issues.issue: Clause 15.6.1 bullet 1 allows AnyValueOrNone in character string templates only on the left hand side, yet rule f) defines a right hand side result for it; it is unclear whether such a reference is allowed.
readings: A right hand side reference to an element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone SHALL yield a pattern "?" with ifpresent.
A right hand side reference to an element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone SHALL cause an error, and rule f) is unreachable.

issues.canonical: If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute, a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL be resolved only if the index is less than the maximum allowed length.
issues.original: g) If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute, the reference shall be resolved only if the referenced element is less than the maximum allowed length.
issues.issue: 'the referenced element is less than the maximum allowed length' means the index of the referenced element.

issues.canonical: If the referenced template has the present restriction, or the referenced field is unrestricted and represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL have the present restriction.
issues.original: i) If the referenced template has the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or if the referenced field is unrestricted and represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result shall have the present restriction.
issues.issue: The sentence is garbled ('..., a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or if ...'); the fragment about a matching symbol was read as a parenthetical description of the present restriction.
readings: If the referenced template has the present restriction (or the referenced field is an unrestricted mandatory field or a field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array), the result SHALL have the present restriction.

If the referenced template has the present restriction or contains a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction while being unrestricted in a mandatory field or field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result SHALL have the present restriction.

issues.canonical: When an item of a binary string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the number of items in the specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.
issues.original: a) When referencing an item of a binary string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is non-negative and less than the number of items in the specific value, the referenced item shall be replaced with the item from the right hand sign of the assignment.
issues.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

issues.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.
issues.original: c) When referencing an item of a character string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is non-negative and less than the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the referenced item shall be replaced with the item from the right hand sign of the assignment.
issues.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

issues.canonical: When an item at index n of a character string template containing a pattern is assigned and n is greater than or equal to the number of items in the pattern, ? metacharacters SHALL first be appended to the pattern as many times as the difference between n and the number of items, and then the item from the right hand side SHALL be appended to the pattern.
issues.original: g) When referencing an item at the index n of a character string template to which a pattern is assigned, if the index is greater than or equal to the number of items in the pattern, first as many ? metacharacters shall be appended to the pattern as is the difference between n and the number of items in the pattern and then the item from the right hand sign of the assignment shall be appended to the pattern.
issues.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

issues.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index used on the right hand side of an assignment is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length of the referenced template.
issues.original: If the index is used on the right hand side of an assignment and is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length.
issues.issue: 'maximum allowed length' presumably refers to the length matching attribute, but the example (v_oct1[10] on a 2-octet specific value without length attribute) treats an index beyond the actual value length as an error too.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a right hand side index is greater than or equal to the maximum length given by the length matching attribute.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a right hand side index is greater than or equal to the number of items of the referenced string template (or its maximum length).

issues.canonical: Referencing a subfield within a structured field to which the ifpresent matching attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended.
issues.original: c) Ifpresent attribute: referencing a subfield within a structured field to which the ifpresent attribute is attached, shall cause an error (irrespective of the value or the matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended).
issues.issue: 'ifpresent attribute' is used for the 'ifpresent matching attribute'.

issues.canonical: Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a template list, a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: b) Template lists, complemented lists, subset and superset: referencing an element within a record of or set of field to which a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned, shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The item heading names template lists, but the rule sentence only lists complemented list, subset and superset; Example 1 shows a template list causing the error. Chose the reading that includes template lists.
readings: Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a template list, a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.
Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.

issues.canonical: The record of element indexes covered by a permutation SHALL be determined by the number of elements of the permutation.
issues.original: Indexes of elements sheltered by a permutation shall be determined based on the number of permutation elements.
issues.issue: "Sheltered" is not a defined term; it is unclear whether the sentence defines which indexes fall inside the permutation, or how the indexes of elements following the permutation are counted. Chose the first reading (Example 4 is consistent with both).
readings: The record of element indexes covered by a permutation SHALL be the consecutive indexes starting at the position of the permutation, one per permutation element.
The indexes of the elements following a permutation SHALL be computed by counting each permutation element as one index.

issues.canonical: A permutation that contains AnyElementsOrNone as a permutation element IS considered to cover all record of element indexes from its position onward.
issues.original: AnyElementsOrNone as a permutation element causes that the permutation shelters all record of element indexes.
issues.issue: "all record of element indexes" can mean every index of the template or every index starting at the permutation position. Chose the second reading.
readings: A permutation containing AnyElementsOrNone covers all record of element indexes from the position of the permutation onward.
A permutation containing AnyElementsOrNone covers all record of element indexes of the template, including those before the permutation.

issues.canonical: If the upper bound of the length restriction of an AnyElementsOrNone is greater than its lower bound, the sequence of AnyElement symbols in the transformed form SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.
issues.original: If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the sequence shall be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.
issues.issue: The text says "lower bound is greater than the upper bound", which is impossible for a valid length restriction; Example 5 ({1, * length(1..3), 5} becomes {1, ?, * length(0..2), 5}) shows the upper bound greater than the lower bound is meant. Chose the example-consistent reading.
readings: If the upper bound is greater than the lower bound, the AnyElement sequence SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction.
If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the AnyElement sequence SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction.

issues.canonical: When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position and the referenced item is a result of transformation, the AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the original template IS replaced with its transformed form and the assignment IS performed afterwards.
issues.original: If the referenced element was a result of transformation, then the AnyValueOrNone symbol in the original template is replaced with its transformed form and the assignment is performed afterwards. When the reference is used at the left hand side of the assignment, the following applies: If positions of all AnyElementsOrNone matching symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item the following rules are used.
issues.issue: The sentence names the AnyValueOrNone symbol, but the transformation applies to AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction (see Example 8).

issues.canonical: The appended AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS given the original length restriction adjusted by the difference between the size of the template before and after the assignment.
issues.original: In such a case, the appended symbol contains the original length restriction adjusted by the difference between the size of the template before and after assignment. If the original AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction, the symbol is appended only if the restriction included items beyond the referenced item.
issues.issue: It is not stated how the bounds are adjusted (e.g. whether the lower bound is clamped at zero) nor how the template size is counted. Example 10 ({1, * length(1..5)} with v_roI[2] := 3 gives * length(0..3)) suggests both bounds are reduced by the number of added elements, with the lower bound not below zero.
readings: Both bounds of the original restriction are reduced by the number of elements added by the assignment, with the lower bound not going below zero.
Both bounds are reduced by the difference in the number of template symbols before and after the assignment, which may yield a negative lower bound.

issues.canonical: Referencing a signature parameter of a signature template to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: a) Value lists and complemented lists: referencing a parameter of a signature template to which a value list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.
issues.issue: "Value list" is used where the matching mechanism is called template list in clause B.1.2.1.

issues.canonical: When a signature parameter of a signature template to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the signature template IS implicitly expanded to the parameter level.
issues.original: b) _AnyValue: when referencing a parameter within a signature to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand_ side of an assignment, the signature template is implicitly expanded to the parameter level.
issues.issue: "within a signature" is used where the signature template is meant.

issues.canonical: Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which template lists or complemented template lists are assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The sentence names only a "union template field", while item a) otherwise covers "union template or template field"; it is unclear whether a union template (not a field) with a template list is also covered.
readings: Referencing an alternative of a union template or union template field to which a template list or complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

Referencing an alternative of a union template field (but not of a top-level union template) to which a template list or complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

issues.canonical: Referencing an element within a map template or field to which `omit` is assigned SHALL follow the rules specified in clause 6.2.15.7.
issues.original: a) _Omit: referencing an element within a map to which omit is assigned shall follow the rules specified in_ clause 6.2.15.7.
issues.issue: "within a map" is used where a map template or field is meant (omit cannot be assigned to a map value).

issues.canonical: Referencing an element within a map template or field to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: b) Template lists and complemented lists: referencing an element within a map field to which a list or complemented list is assigned, shall cause an error.
issues.issue: "list" is used for template list, and "map field" is used although Example 1 applies the rule to a map template variable.

issues.canonical: After the assignment to a non-present element of a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added to the map template.
issues.original: Then the value or matching mechanism at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced field and AnyElementsOrNone shall be added to the map template. When referencing an element of a map template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone, if the referenced element is not present and the reference occurs on the left-hand side of an assignment, the template or field is implicitly expanded recursively up to and including, the depth of the referenced subfield and AnyValue is assigned to the referenced field.
issues.issue: The map template already contains AnyElementsOrNone; it is unclear whether a second AnyElementsOrNone is added or the existing one is kept.
readings: The map template SHALL contain AnyElementsOrNone after the assignment (the existing one is kept).
A further AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added to the map template in addition to the existing one.

issues.canonical: Certain matching mechanisms MAY be used in combination with each other.
issues.original: Some of the mechanisms may be used in combination.
issues.issue: "Some of the mechanisms" does not state which mechanisms can be combined; the first reading (only combinations defined in annex B) is chosen because restriction a) forbids all applications not allowed by table 11.
readings: Only the combinations of matching mechanisms explicitly defined in annex B (e.g. length restriction with AnyElementsOrNone, ifpresent with other mechanisms) MAY be used together.
Any matching mechanisms MAY be combined unless a combination is explicitly forbidden.

issues.canonical: When matching, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
issues.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.
issues.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing `omit` is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.
readings: `omit` assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
`omit` assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.

issues.canonical: When matching, AnyValueOrNone (`*`) SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
issues.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.
issues.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing AnyValueOrNone (`*`) is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.
readings: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
AnyValueOrNone (`*`) assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.

issues.canonical: When matching, `ifpresent` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set types, regardless of the type of that field.
issues.original: However when matching, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set types only (without restriction on the type of that field). NOTE 1: Can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set templates.
issues.issue: "it shall be applied ... only" in combination with NOTE 1 allowing assignment to whole templates leaves open whether matching against a whole template containing `ifpresent` is an error or simply never applies; the restriction reading is chosen.
readings: `ifpresent` assigned to a whole template SHALL NOT be used in a matching operation (e.g. receive) at all; it may only be applied when matching optional fields of record and set types.
`ifpresent` assigned to a whole template is allowed and only matches optional fields of record and set types when it is used inside such a template.

issues.canonical: A template or template field of a `set of` type MAY use the matching mechanisms SpecificValue, Omit (subject to NOTE 1), ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue (`?`), AnyValueOrNone (`*`), Superset, Subset, AnyElement (`?`), AnyElementsOrNone (`*`), LengthRestriction and IfPresent (subject to NOTE 1).
issues.original: Col1: set of; Col2: Yes; Table 11: TTCN-3 Matching Mechanisms: Yes1; Col4: Yes; Col5: Yes; Col6: Yes; Col7: Yes; Col9: Yes; Col10: Yes; Col13: Yes; Col14: Yes; Col16: Yes; Col17: Yes1
issues.issue: The set of row shows 'Yes' instead of 'Yes1' for AnyValueOrNone, unlike all other rows; the second reading is assumed to be intended but the canonical follows the table as printed.
readings: AnyValueOrNone for a set of type is allowed without the restrictions of NOTE 1 (as printed).
AnyValueOrNone for a set of type is subject to NOTE 1 like for all other types, and the missing footnote marker is an editorial omission.

issues.canonical: The range matching mechanism `(lowerBound .. upperBound)` matches integer or float values between and including the lower bound and the upper bound.
issues.original: **(lowerBound** `..` _upperBound): a range of integer or float values between and including the lower- and upper_ bounds;
issues.issue: The description mentions only integer and float values, while table 11 also allows Range for character strings; the second reading is consistent with table 11 and annex B, but the canonical keeps the stated integer/float semantics.
readings: The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values only.
The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values and, as allowed by table 11, also to character string values.

issues.canonical: The AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any number of consecutive elements in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value, or no element at all.
issues.original: ***: wildcard for any number of consecutive elements in a string, array,** `record of or set of, or no` element at all (i.e. an omitted element);
issues.issue: "omitted element" suggests the special value omit, while what is meant is the absence of any element.

issues.canonical: The `ifpresent` matching attribute matches an optional field that is omitted, and applies the matching of the template it is attached to when the optional field is present.
issues.original: **ifpresent: for matching of optional field values (if not omitted).**
issues.issue: "for matching of optional field values (if not omitted)" does not say what happens with an omitted field; the first reading is chosen as it is consistent with annex B.1.4.2 and NOTE 2.
readings: `ifpresent` matches an omitted optional field, and otherwise matches the present value against the template it is attached to.
`ifpresent` is used only for matching present (not omitted) optional field values.

issues.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
issues.original: (omit) the template shall resolve to a value matching mechanism (i.e. the fields of it shall resolve to a specific value or omit, and the whole template may also resolve to omit).
issues.issue: The undefined term 'value matching mechanism' is used; the explanation in parentheses shows that a specific value (or omit for the whole template) is meant.

issues.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction CAN be used to define a field of a record or set template.
issues.original: Such a template can be used to define a field of a record and set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.
issues.issue: 'record and set template' means a record template or a set template.

issues.canonical: A record or set template whose field is defined by a template with the `omit` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
issues.original: Such a template can be used to define a field of a record and set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.
issues.issue: 'send statement' is used for the send operation; 'record and set template' means record or set template.

issues.canonical: A record or set template whose mandatory field is defined by a template with the `value` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
issues.original: It can be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.
issues.issue: 'send statement' is used for the send operation.

issues.canonical: A restricted or unrestricted template SHALL be used as actual parameter of a formal template parameter, or assigned to a template or template variable, only as permitted by table 13.
issues.original: b) Restricted and unrestricted templates maybe used as actual parameters of formal template parameters or assigned to templates or template variables according to table 13.
issues.issue: 'maybe' is a misspelling of 'may be'.

issues.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL NOT use the matching mechanisms ComplementedList, TemplateList, AnyValue, AnyValueOrNone, Range, Superset, Subset, Pattern, match decoded content (`decmatch`), AnyElement, AnyElementsOrNone, Permutation, LengthRestriction or IfPresent.
issues.original: Used with template restriction: omit; Value: Yes; Instead of values: Yes
