issues.original: When the any from component array notation is used, the components from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for being inactive or running a function from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
issues.issue: The components are said to be checked for 'being inactive or running a function', which conflicts with 21.3.5-s004 (a stopped alive-type component is also alive) and ignores altstep behaviours. The reading consistent with the alive semantics of single components is chosen.
readings: With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked for being alive as defined for a single component (for alive-type PTCs, inactive, running or stopped), iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.
With `any from`, each component of the array IS checked only for being inactive or running a function, iterating from innermost to outermost dimension and from lowest to highest index.

issues.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `@index` clause of an `alive` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the index value assigned to it IS the value produced by the `alive` operation; a later evaluation of the variable does not invoke the `alive` operation again.
issues.original: f) If a variable referenced in the @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the alive operation.
issues.issue: The text says 'the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the alive operation', but the @index clause receives the index of the found component, not the Boolean result. The reading that the stored index value is meant is chosen.
readings: A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the index value determined by the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.
A lazy or fuzzy variable referenced in the `@index` clause IS assigned the Boolean result of the `alive` operation, and later evaluation of it does not invoke the `alive` operation again.

issues.canonical: The `running` operation IS a boolean expression that returns a boolean value indicating whether the specified test component (or all test components) is still executing.
issues.original: The running operation is considered to be a boolean expression and, thus, returns a boolean value to indicate whether the specified test component (or all test components) has terminated.
issues.issue: The sentence says the result indicates whether the component "has terminated", which contradicts s004/s005 where true means still executing; the reading consistent with s004 was chosen.
readings: The `running` operation returns `true` if the specified test component is still executing.
The `running` operation returns a value indicating whether the specified test component has terminated (true meaning terminated).

issues.canonical: `all component.running` returns `true` if all PTCs that have been started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.
issues.original: When the all keyword is used with the running operation, it will return true if all PTCs started but not stopped explicitly by another component are executing their behaviour.
issues.issue: It is unclear whether PTCs that terminated on their own (not stopped explicitly by another component) are excluded or make the result false.
readings: `all component.running` returns `true` if every started PTC, except those stopped explicitly by another component, is still executing.
`all component.running` returns `true` only if every started PTC is still executing, regardless of how it stopped.

issues.canonical: The size of the integer array or record of integer type used in the index redirection SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
issues.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
issues.issue: "size ... the same as the dimension" could mean the number of dimensions or the size of a dimension.
readings: The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the component array.
The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the component array.

issues.canonical: The `done` operation SHALL be applied to PTCs only.
issues.original: a) The done operation can be used for PTCs only.
issues.issue: "can be used for PTCs only" is phrased as a capability but is meant as a restriction.

issues.canonical: The size of the integer array or record of integer type used in the index redirection SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
issues.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
issues.issue: "size ... the same as the dimension" could mean the number of dimensions or the size of a dimension.
readings: The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the component array.
The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the component array.

issues.canonical: A `killed` operation applied to a non-alive test component matches if the component stopped (implicitly or explicitly) the execution of its behaviour or has been killed explicitly, i.e. it is equivalent to the `done` operation.
issues.original: NOTE 1: When checking normal test components a killed operation matches if it stopped (implicitly or explicitly) the execution of its behaviour or has been killed explicitly, i.e. the operation is equivalent to the done operation (see clause 21.3.7).
issues.issue: "normal test components" is used for non-alive test components; "it" refers to the checked component, not the operation.

issues.canonical: `all component.killed` matches if all PTCs of the test case have ceased to exist.
issues.original: When the all keyword is used with the killed operation, it matches if all PTCs of the test case have ceased to exist.
issues.issue: "test case" is written instead of the keyword-style term "testcase" used for the TTCN-3 construct.

issues.canonical: The `killed` operation SHALL be applied to PTCs only.
issues.original: a) The killed operation can be used for PTCs only.
issues.issue: "can be used for PTCs only" is phrased as a capability but is meant as a restriction.

issues.canonical: The size of the integer array or record of integer type used in the index redirection SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the multi-dimensional component array.
issues.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional component arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
issues.issue: "size ... the same as the dimension" could mean the number of dimensions or the size of a dimension.
readings: The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the component array.
The size of the integer array or record of integer SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the component array.

issues.canonical: The execution of the started test behaviour IS complete when the started function terminates by executing a `return` statement or by reaching the end of its function body.
issues.original: Complete execution occurs when the started function is terminated by executing a return statement or if it reaches the end of the function body.
issues.issue: The rule only mentions functions although the call operation also accepts altstep instances (see the example a_myFourthBehaviour); the first reading is chosen as altsteps are explicitly allowed.
readings: The execution of a called function is complete when it executes a `return` statement or reaches the end of its body; the execution of a called altstep is complete when the altstep terminates normally after executing one of its alternatives.
Only called functions can have a complete execution; a called altstep execution is always incomplete.

issues.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the called component SHALL be implicitly stopped.
issues.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.
issues.issue: Typo 'timout' for 'timeout'.

issues.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the StatementBlock of the `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL be executed before the `call` operation terminates.
issues.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.
issues.issue: Typo 'timout' for 'timeout'.

issues.canonical: A `call` operation SHALL NOT be applied to a test component that is not created alive and has already been started or called once, nor to a test component that has been killed.
issues.original: If the called component is not created alive and has already been started or called once or if it has been killed, additional call operations are not allowed.
issues.issue: The scope of 'or if it has been killed' is unclear; the first reading is chosen since a killed component of any kind cannot execute behaviour. The text also does not say whether violation is a compile-time or runtime error; the example shows it is a test case error.
readings: A call operation is not allowed on a killed test component (alive or not) and on a non-alive test component that has already been started or called once.
A call operation is not allowed on a non-alive test component that has already been started, called or killed; the killed condition only applies to non-alive components.

issues.canonical: The function or altstep invoked in a `call` operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible.
issues.original: b) The function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7).
issues.issue: 'runs on definition' is used instead of the usual 'runs on clause', and 'call test component operation' instead of 'call operation'.

issues.canonical: The return type of the function invoked in a `call` operation SHALL be a component data type.
issues.original: d) The return value of the function invoked from a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.
issues.issue: The restriction concerns the return type, but 'return value' is used.

issues.canonical: The optional SimpleExpression giving the timeout duration of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `float`.
issues.original: e) The optional SimpleExpression representing the timer value shall be of a float type.
issues.issue: The semantic description calls it 'timeout duration', the restriction 'timer value' although no timer is involved.

issues.canonical: A `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL NOT be present in a `call` operation unless a timeout duration is given.
issues.original: f) The optional catch `timeout clause may be present only if the timeout value has been defined.`
issues.issue: 'timeout value' is used instead of 'timeout duration'.

issues.canonical: The variable in the `value` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be compatible with the return type of the invoked function.
issues.original: g) The variable in the value clause shall be compatible with the return value of the invoked function.
issues.issue: Compatibility is a property of types; 'return value' is used where the return type is meant.

issues.canonical: The `receive` operation IS blocking: the receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until it processes the received message.
issues.original: The RECEIVER is blocked on the receive operation until it processes the received message.
issues.issue: 'until it processes the received message' does not state whether the message must match; chosen reading: blocked until a matching message is processed (consistent with the alt/snapshot semantics in clause 20).
readings: The receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until a matching message has been received and processed.
The receiver is blocked on the `receive` operation until any message arrives in the port queue.

issues.canonical: When the `trigger` operation is executed, a message at the top of the port queue that does not fulfil the matching criteria IS removed from the port queue without any further action.
issues.original: Messages at the top of the queue that do not fulfil the matching criteria are removed from the port without any further action.
issues.issue: messages are removed from the port queue, not from the port itself.

issues.canonical: The `send` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Send message; Col2: send; Col3: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `send` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `send` at procedure-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `receive` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Receive message; Col2: receive; Col3: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `receive` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `receive` at procedure-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `trigger` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Trigger on message; Col2: trigger; Col3: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `trigger` operation SHALL NOT be used at procedure-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `trigger` at procedure-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `call` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Invoke procedure call; Col2: call; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `call` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `call` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `getcall` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Accept procedure call from remote entity; Col2: getcall; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `getcall` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `getcall` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `reply` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Reply to procedure call from remote entity; Col2: reply; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `reply` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `reply` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `raise` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Raise exception (to an accepted call); Col2: raise; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `raise` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `raise` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `getreply` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Handle response from a previous call; Col2: getreply; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `getreply` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `getreply` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: The `catch` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
issues.original: Table 22: Overview of TTCN-3 communication operations: Catch exception (from called entity); Col2: catch; Col4: Yes
issues.issue: the restriction is derived from an empty table cell; chosen reading: empty cell means not allowed, as clause 22.0 says the table summarizes restrictions on usage.
readings: The `catch` operation SHALL NOT be used at message-based ports.
Table 22 makes no statement about the use of `catch` at message-based ports.

issues.canonical: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the caller MAY handle an exception by using a `catch` operation in an `alt` statement.
issues.original: The CALLER may handle the exception by using a catch operation in an alt statement.
issues.issue: 'may' can mean that handling the exception is optional, or restrict where the catch is placed; chosen reading: handling is optional and an alt statement is one possible place.
readings: In non-blocking procedure-based communication, the caller MAY handle an exception by using a `catch` operation in an `alt` statement (and also elsewhere, e.g. as stand-alone statement).
In non-blocking procedure-based communication, a `catch` operation handling an exception of a non-blocking call SHALL be used within an `alt` statement.

issues.canonical: When unicast, multicast or broadcast communication is used via a mapped port, one, several or all entities within the SUT CAN be reached via the specified mapped port.
issues.original: In this case, one, several or all entities within the SUT can be reached via the specified mapped port.
issues.issue: 'entities within the SUT' is not defined; the addressable entities are presumably those identified by the address type at the test system interface.

issues.canonical: The send part of a sending operation SHALL define the message or procedure call to be transmitted.
issues.original: defines the message or procedure call to be transmitted;
issues.issue: The send part of a reply or raise operation transmits a reply or an exception, not a message or procedure call; the list is incomplete.

improper_terms.proper: message, procedure call, reply or exception

issues.canonical: A sending operation SHALL contain the port name, the operation name and the value to be sent.
issues.original: The port name, operation name and value shall be present in all sending operations.
issues.issue: "value" is used where a template instance (e.g. a signature template for call) is meant.

issues.canonical: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL be present when the called procedure returns a value or has `out` or `inout` parameters whose values are needed within the calling component.
issues.original: The response and exception handling part of the call operation is optional and is required for cases where the called procedure returns a value or has out or inout parameters whose values are needed within the calling component and for cases where the called procedure may raise exceptions which need to be handled by the calling component.
issues.issue: "is required" may be a normative obligation or merely a usage hint; the reading as a usage hint was chosen for testability, the canonical keeps the literal text.
readings: The response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL be present when the return value or out/inout parameter values are needed by the calling component.
A `call` operation without a response and exception handling part CANNOT make the return value or out/inout parameter values available to the calling component.

issues.canonical: The identification of the communication partner (`from` clause) in a receiving operation NEED NOT be specified except in one-to-many connections where the communication partner needs to be explicitly identified.
issues.original: The identification of the communication partner (denoted by the from keyword) is optional and need only be specified in cases of one-to-many connections where the receiving entity needs to be explicitly identified.
issues.issue: The text says "receiving entity" although the entity identified by the from clause is the sending communication partner.

issues.canonical: For procedure-based ports, the assignment part of a receiving operation stores the `in` and `inout` parameters of an accepted call, the return value or the exception.
issues.original: In the case of procedure-based ports it is used for storing the in and inout parameters of an accepted call, for storing the return value or for storing exceptions.
issues.issue: Only getcall stores in/inout parameters; getreply stores out/inout parameters, which the sentence does not mention. Chosen reading: the text lists examples per operation kind.
readings: The assignment part of a getcall operation stores in and inout parameters, that of a getreply operation the return value (and out/inout parameters), and that of a catch operation the exception.
The assignment part of any procedure-based receiving operation stores only in and inout parameters, return values or exceptions.

issues.canonical: Strong typing IS NOT required for the message or parameter value assignment part of a receiving operation.
issues.original: For the message or parameter value assignment part strong typing is not required, e.g. the variable used for storing a message shall be type-compatible to the type of the incoming message.
issues.issue: "strong typing is not required" followed by "e.g. ... shall be type-compatible" is contradictory in wording; chosen reading: type compatibility instead of type identity is sufficient.
readings: The variable in a value or parameter assignment SHALL be type-compatible with, but need not be of the same type as, the received value.
No type check is performed for value or parameter assignments of a receiving operation.

issues.canonical: No AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `send` operation SHALL contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
issues.original: No AddressRef in the to clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.
issues.issue: The consequence of a null AddressRef at runtime is not stated; chosen reading: it is a runtime error (test case error).
readings: Executing a `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef SHALL cause a test case error.
A `send` operation whose `to` clause contains a `null` AddressRef is undefined behaviour left to the tool.

issues.canonical: The optional type part of the matching criteria of a `receive` operation SHALL be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.
issues.original: An optional type field in the matching criteria to the receive operation shall be used to avoid any ambiguity of the type of the value being received.
issues.issue: 'type field' is used for the optional Type ':' prefix of the in-line template, which restriction a) calls 'type part'; 'field' could be confused with a record field.

issues.canonical: If the match is successful, the received value or parts of it CAN be stored in variables or formal parameters.
issues.original: If the match is successful, the value is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored in variables or formal parameters.
issues.issue: 'is removed from the port queue and/or parts of this value can be stored' mixes the always-happening removal with the optional storing; the 'and/or' scope is unclear. Chosen reading: removal always happens, storing is optional.
readings: If the match is successful, the message is removed from the port queue and the whole value or parts of it CAN additionally be stored in variables or formal parameters.
If the match is successful, either the message is removed from the port queue or parts of it are stored, or both.

issues.canonical: An encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause with a value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error is not specified.
readings: A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
A disallowed encoding format value SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is known statically, and a test case error otherwise.

issues.canonical: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the variable following the `sender` keyword.
issues.original: When the message is received on a connected port, only the component reference is stored in the following the sender keyword, but the test system shall internally store the component name too, if any (to be used in logging).
issues.issue: The sentence is garbled ('stored in the following the sender keyword'); the noun 'variable or formal parameter' is missing.

improper_terms.used: stored in the following the sender keyword
improper_terms.proper: stored in the variable or formal parameter following the sender keyword

issues.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports are iterated from innermost to outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
issues.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
issues.issue: 'from innermost to outermost' could mean the innermost (last) index varies fastest, or that the innermost dimension is the outer loop; the example order [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1] supports the first reading, which is chosen.
readings: The last (innermost) index varies fastest: [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The first index varies fastest: [0][0], [1][0], [0][1], [1][1].

issues.canonical: A `receive` operation SHALL NOT bind incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template.
issues.original: c) No binding of the incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template shall occur.
issues.issue: It is unclear what 'binding to the terms of the expression or to the template' means for a test author.
readings: Matching a received message SHALL NOT assign values to variables used in the template or expression (no unification-like binding).
Variables referenced in the template or expression SHALL NOT be changed by the receive operation except through the redirect clauses.

issues.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: e) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.
issues.issue: Kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not specified.
readings: A type mismatch detectable statically SHALL cause a compile-time error.
A type mismatch SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.

issues.canonical: A type mismatch at storing the sender SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: e) Type mismatch at storing the received value or parts of the received value and storing the sender shall cause an error.
issues.issue: Kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not specified.
readings: A sender type mismatch detectable statically SHALL cause a compile-time error.
A sender type mismatch SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.

issues.canonical: If the `receive` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or formal parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the address expression in the `from` clause.
issues.original: l) If the receive operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.
issues.issue: The from clause contains AddressRef items, not a template; 'parameter' should be 'formal parameter'.

issues.canonical: The referenced value or the return type of the function instance preceding the `receive` keyword SHALL be of a port type.
issues.original: n) The referenced value associated with ValueRef or the return type associated with FunctionInstance followed by the receive keyword, shall be of a port type.
issues.issue: The syntax block uses ObjectReference, not ValueRef or FunctionInstance.

issues.canonical: A `trigger` operation SHALL specify the port name and matching criteria for type and value.
issues.original: The trigger operation requires the port name, matching criteria for type and value, an optional from restriction (i.e. selection of communication partner) and an optional assignment of the matching message and sender component to variables.
issues.issue: The sentence says matching criteria are required, but clause 'Trigger on any message' allows a trigger without argument list. Chosen reading: the matching criteria are required unless the trigger on any message form is used.
readings: A `trigger` operation SHALL always specify matching criteria for type and value.
A `trigger` operation SHALL specify matching criteria for type and value unless it is a trigger on any message without argument list.

issues.canonical: A `trigger` operation with no template instance SHALL trigger on the receipt of any message.
issues.original: A trigger operation with no argument list shall trigger on the receipt of any message.
issues.issue: 'argument list' is used for the optional TemplateInstance of the trigger operation.

issues.canonical: Every AddressRef item in the `from` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
issues.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.
issues.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

issues.canonical: Every ValueRef item in the `sender` clause of a `trigger` operation SHALL be of type `address`, a component type, or the address type bound to the port type of the referenced port instance.
issues.original: d) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause C.5) of the port instance referenced in the trigger operation.
issues.issue: 'component' is used where 'component type' is meant.

issues.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the port array.
issues.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional port arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the array.
issues.issue: 'the dimension of the respective array' is read as the number of dimensions (supported by example 5: p[10][10] with v_i[2]).
readings: The size of the integer array SHALL equal the number of dimensions of the port array.
The size of the integer array SHALL equal the size of a dimension of the port array.

issues.canonical: If a `trigger` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the AddressRef in the `from` clause.
issues.original: j) If the trigger operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.
issues.issue: 'template in the from clause' is used although the from clause contains AddressRef items (address or component references), not templates.

issues.canonical: A snapshot taken for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY include the top element of the port over which the procedure has been called, if any.
issues.original: This means a corresponding snapshot includes all information necessary to evaluate the (optional) Boolean guards, may include the top element (if any) of the port over which the procedure has been called and may include a timeout exception generated by the (optional) timer that supervises the call.
issues.issue: 'may include' could mean the snapshot only contains the port top element if present, or that inclusion is optional for the tool; the reading 'includes it if present' is chosen.
readings: A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL include the top element of the calling port if the queue is not empty.
A snapshot for the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation MAY optionally include the top element of the calling port.

issues.canonical: If the `nowait` keyword is used in a `call` operation, a response or exception of the called procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.
issues.original: If the nowait keyword is used, a possible response or exception of the called procedure has to be removed from the port queue by using a getreply or a catch operation in a subsequent alt statement.
issues.issue: Unclear whether this is a requirement on the test writer (error if not removed) or a description of the only way to remove such entries; the description reading is chosen as primary.
readings: A response or exception to a `nowait` call can only be removed from the port queue by a `getreply` or `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` statement.
A test SHALL handle every response or exception of a `nowait` call in a subsequent `alt` statement, otherwise an error occurs.

issues.canonical: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
issues.original: Possible exceptions raised by non-blocking procedures have to be removed from the port queue by using catch operations in subsequent alt or interleave statements.
issues.issue: Same as for nowait calls: obligation on the test writer vs. description of the only removal mechanism; obligation reading chosen.
readings: An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure SHALL be removed by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.
An exception raised by a non-blocking procedure CAN only be removed from the port queue by a `catch` operation in a subsequent `alt` or `interleave` statement.

issues.canonical: The port type definition of the port used in a `call` operation SHALL include the signature of the called procedure in its out or inout list.
issues.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the call operation belongs in its out or inout list i.e. it shall be allowed to call this procedure at this port.
issues.issue: 'name of the procedure' is used where 'signature' is meant; 'out or inout list' refers to the out/inout direction lists of the port type.

issues.canonical: In a `call` operation, only out parameters of the signature MAY be omitted or specified with a matching mechanism.
issues.original: c) Only out parameters may be omitted or specified with a matching attribute.
issues.issue: 'matching attribute' is used instead of 'matching mechanism'; 'omitted' refers to the not-used symbol '-'.

issues.canonical: Each AddressRef in the `to` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `call` operation.
issues.original: f) All AddressRef items in the to clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the call operation.
issues.issue: 'component' is used where 'a component type' is meant.

issues.canonical: An unqualified `getreply` or `catch` operation in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation SHALL only treat replies from and exceptions raised by the called procedure.
issues.original: Unqualified getreply and catch operations shall only treat replies from and exceptions raised by the called procedure.
issues.issue: 'Unqualified' is not defined here; it may mean without a signature/from clause, or the any-port form. Chosen: operations without a signature-specific filter.
readings: A `getreply`/`catch` without signature reference in a call's handling part SHALL only treat replies/exceptions of the called procedure.
An `any port.getreply`/`any port.catch` in a call's handling part SHALL only treat replies/exceptions of the called procedure.

issues.canonical: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT raise a timeout exception.
issues.original: l) The call operation for a non-blocking procedure shall have no response and exception handling part, shall raise no timeout exception and shall not use the nowait keyword.
issues.issue: 'shall raise no timeout exception' likely means no CallTimerValue shall be given; chosen reading: no timeout value is allowed.
readings: A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT specify a CallTimerValue.
A `call` operation for a non-blocking procedure SHALL NOT generate a timeout exception at runtime even if a timer value is given.

issues.canonical: If the referenced parameter is of the universal charstring type, the `@decoded` clause MAY contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
issues.original: In case the referenced field is of the universal `charstring type, the @decoded` clause can contain an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
issues.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

issues.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause that is not one of the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error is not stated; the most likely reading is a test case error at runtime (the value may be non-constant), but a compile-time error is required when the value is known statically.
readings: An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An encoding format parameter value not allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a compile-time error if it can be determined statically.

issues.canonical: If the referenced parameter is not of the universal charstring type, the encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
issues.original: In case the referenced field is not a universal **charstring, the optional** parameter shall not be present.
issues.issue: The text speaks of a 'referenced field', but in a getcall param clause the referenced item is a signature parameter.

issues.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `getcall` operation SHALL include the signature to which the `getcall` operation belongs in its `in` or `inout` list.
issues.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the getcall operation belongs in its in or inout list.
issues.issue: 'procedure' is used where the signature (procedure signature) is meant.

issues.canonical: The value assignment part (`-> value`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
issues.original: d) The value assignment part shall not be used with the getcall operation.
issues.issue: 'value assignment part' is not defined for getcall; the syntax permits '@index value', so it is unclear what is forbidden. Chosen reading: the value redirect '-> value' known from receive operations.
readings: A value redirect (`-> value VariableRef`) SHALL NOT be used with the `getcall` operation.
No assignment using the `value` keyword (including `@index value`) SHALL be used with the `getcall` operation.

issues.canonical: If the `getcall` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
issues.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the type of the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.
issues.issue: 'the sender' could denote the statically known address type of the port/connection or the actual runtime sender; NOTE 3 suggests a check where the sender type can be determined.
readings: If no `from` clause is present, the type of the sender, where it can be determined statically, SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable (compile-time check).
If no `from` clause is present, the actual sender address at runtime SHALL be type compatible with the type of the `sender` clause variable, otherwise an error occurs.

issues.canonical: An error due to a type mismatch CAN occur if the types in the signature matching part of a `getcall` operation are not compatible to the types in the assignment part, or if the `from` clause is missing and the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
issues.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
issues.issue: NOTE 3 uses 'receive part' in the getcall clause, where the signature matching part (TemplateInstance) is meant.

issues.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `reply` operation SHALL include the signature to which the `reply` operation belongs in its `in` or `inout` list.
issues.original: The type definition of the port shall include the name of the procedure to which the reply operation belongs in its in or inout list.
issues.issue: 'procedure' is used where the signature (procedure signature) is meant.

issues.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or test case error) is not stated; the canonical keeps the generic 'error'.
readings: An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.
An invalid encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause SHALL cause a compile-time error when it is statically known.

issues.canonical: If the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not of the universal charstring type, the optional encoding format parameter of the `@decoded` clause SHALL NOT be present.
issues.original: In case the parameter or referenced field of the return value is not a universal **char string, the** optional parameter shall not be present.
issues.issue: The text writes 'universal char string' (PDF formatting artefact) where the type 'universal charstring' is meant.

issues.canonical: If a get any reply operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, it SHALL only treat replies from the procedure invoked by that `call` operation.
issues.original: If GetAnyReply is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation, it shall only treat replies from the procedure invoked by the call operation.
issues.issue: 'GetAnyReply' is a BNF-style name that is not defined in this clause; the 'get any reply' form of the getreply operation is meant.

improper_terms.proper: get any reply (getreply operation without signature argument)

issues.canonical: If the port array is multi-dimensional, the ports ARE iterated over from the innermost to the outermost array dimension, from lowest to highest index for each dimension (e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1]).
issues.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
issues.issue: 'From innermost to outermost' could be read as the first index varying fastest, but the example sequence shows the last index varying fastest; the canonical follows the example.
readings: The last index varies fastest, as shown by the example sequence [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension (first index) is iterated over first, i.e. the first index varies fastest.

issues.canonical: Parameters or return values of replies accepted by a get any reply operation SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable, i.e. the `param` and `value` clauses SHALL NOT be present.
issues.original: c) Parameters or return values of responses accepted by get any reply shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the **param and value clause shall not be present.**
issues.issue: 'responses' is used where 'replies' is meant.

issues.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the same as the number of dimensions of the respective port array.
issues.original: h) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
issues.issue: 'the dimension of the respective port array' means the number of dimensions of the port array.

issues.canonical: The optional redirection part of a `catch` operation IS the storing of the exception value and/or one or more of its parts and the retrieval of the address of the component that raised the exception.
issues.original: The (optional) redirection part of the catch operation comprises of storing the exception value and/or one or more parts of it and the retrieval of the address of the calling component.
issues.issue: The exception is raised by the called component; 'calling component' is misleading. The `sender` clause retrieves the address of the component that raised the exception, as stated in the next sentence.

improper_terms.proper: sender (the component that raised the exception)

issues.canonical: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: Any other value shall cause an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error (static or dynamic) is not specified; the canonical text keeps the generic 'error'.
readings: An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a compile-time error if it is known at compile time and a runtime error otherwise.
An encoding format parameter value of the `@decoded` clause other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause a test case error at runtime.

issues.canonical: If a `catch` operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, the port name and signature reference IS redundant information, because it follows from the `call` operation.
issues.original: If the catch operation is used in the accepting part of a call operation, the information about port name and signature reference to indicate the procedure that raised the exception is redundant, because this information follows from the call operation.
issues.issue: The call operation part is called 'response and exception handling part' elsewhere in the clause.

issues.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `catch` operation SHALL include in its `out` or `inout` list the signature to which the caught exception belongs.
issues.original: b) The type definition of the port shall include in its out or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.
issues.issue: Port type lists contain signature references; 'procedure' is used loosely for the signature.

issues.canonical: The assignment of exception values to variables SHALL be made in the redirection (assignment) part of the `catch` operation.
issues.original: The assignment of the exception values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the catch operation.
issues.issue: The syntax and the semantic description call this the redirection part.

issues.canonical: A `catch` operation for the timeout exception SHALL only be used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
issues.original: d) Catching timeout exceptions shall be restricted to the exception handling part of a call.
issues.issue: Elsewhere the clause uses 'response and exception handling part'.

improper_terms.used: exception handling part of a call
improper_terms.proper: response and exception handling part of a call operation

issues.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or, if the `from` clause is missing, if the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
issues.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.
issues.issue: The note is copied from the receive operation; for catch the 'receive part' is the exception matching part.

improper_terms.proper: matching part (signature and template instance) of the catch operation

issues.canonical: The value referenced by the ObjectReference before the `catch` keyword, or the return type of a function instance used there, SHALL be of a port type.
issues.original: o) The referenced value associated with Ref or the return type associated with FunctionInstance followed by the catch keyword, shall be of a port type.
issues.issue: The syntactical structure of the catch operation uses ObjectReference; Ref and FunctionInstance do not appear in it.

issues.canonical: A `check` operation on any port of a specific port array IS denoted by the `any from` PortArrayRef syntax.
issues.original: To check on any port from a specific port array, indices use the any from PortArrayRef syntax where PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a port array identifier. **Check on any port from a port array**
issues.issue: The phrase 'from a specific port array, indices use' is garbled; the word 'indices' appears to be an editorial leftover.

issues.canonical: For a multi-dimensional port array, the `check` operation iterates over the ports from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
issues.original: If the port array is multi-dimensional, then the ports are iterated over from innermost to outermost array dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension, e.g. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
issues.issue: 'From innermost to outermost dimension' can be read either way; the given example sequence fixes the rightmost-index-fastest order, which is chosen.
readings: The `check` operation iterates such that the last (rightmost) index varies fastest, i.e. [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The `check` operation iterates such that the first (leftmost) index varies fastest, i.e. [0][0], [1][0], [0][1], [1][1].

issues.canonical: Using the `check` operation in a wrong manner, e.g. checking for an exception at a message-based port, SHALL cause a test case error.
issues.original: a) Using the check operation in a wrong manner, e.g. check for an exception at a message-based port shall cause a test case error.
issues.issue: 'Wrong manner' is only illustrated by one example, and NOTE 3 says most misuse can be detected statically; the literal reading (test case error) is chosen.
readings: Any misuse of the `check` operation (e.g. a `catch` on a message-based port) SHALL cause a runtime test case error.
Misuse of the `check` operation that can be detected statically SHALL be rejected at compile time; only remaining misuse SHALL cause a test case error.

issues.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the port array.
issues.original: f) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
issues.issue: 'The same as the dimension of the respective port array' means the number of dimensions of the port array.

issues.canonical: If the `check` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
issues.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.
issues.issue: 'The sender' is not specified as a value or a type; NOTE 4 suggests a check whenever the sender type can be determined, so the first reading is chosen.
readings: The type of the actual sender (address or component reference determined at runtime) SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.

The address type associated with the port (address type bound to the port type, or the component type) SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause, checked statically.

issues.canonical: A `start` operation applied to an unstopped port restarts the port by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
issues.original: The start port operation will cause unstopped ports to be restarted by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
issues.issue: 'unstopped ports' is not a defined port state; chose the reading that covers every non-stopped port (started or halted), consistent with NOTE 3 of 22.5.4.
readings: A `start` operation applied to an already started port restarts it by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
A `start` operation applied to a port that is not in the stopped state (started or halted) clears its incoming queue.

issues.canonical: When a port is stopped, all receiving operations at that port performed before the `stop` operation SHALL be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.
issues.original: To cease listening at the port means that all receiving operations defined before the stop operation shall be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.
issues.issue: 'defined before the stop operation' is unclear: executed before in time or written before in the code; chose the temporal execution reading.
readings: Receiving operations already executed (successfully matched) before the `stop` operation are completed, i.e. their effects (e.g. value redirections) take place.
Receiving operations that appear textually before the `stop` operation in the behaviour are performed completely before the port is suspended.

issues.canonical: If a `stop` operation is performed on a halted port before all entries ahead of the halt marker have been processed, further receiving operations SHALL NOT succeed at that port, effective immediately.
issues.original: NOTE 2: If a port stop operation is performed on a halted port before all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, further receive operations are disallowed immediately (i.e. the marker is virtually moved to the top of the queue).
issues.issue: NOTE uses 'receive operations' where the clause otherwise uses 'receiving operations' (covering receive, trigger, getcall etc.).

issues.canonical: Calling the `checkstate` operation with an invalid argument causes an error.
issues.original: Calling the checkstate operation with an invalid argument leads to an error.
issues.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; chose the general reading that an error results, either at compile time for constant arguments or at runtime otherwise.
readings: A `checkstate` call with an argument value not in the allowed list causes a runtime error (the argument may be computed dynamically).
A `checkstate` call with an invalid argument is rejected at compile time when the value is statically known.

issues.canonical: A timer operation MAY be used in a testcase, a function and an altstep.
issues.original: These operations may be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
issues.issue: 'test cases' is used instead of the keyword-level term 'testcase'; the sentence does not mention the module control function, although clause 23.1 states that control components maintain timer lists, so it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive.
readings: A timer operation MAY be used only in a testcase, a function or an altstep.
A timer operation MAY be used in a testcase, a function, an altstep and the module control function.

issues.canonical: The timeout-list IS part of the snapshot taken during the execution of a testcase.
issues.original: The timeout-lists are part of the snapshots that are taken when a test case is executed.
issues.issue: 'test case' is used where the TTCN-3 construct 'testcase' (its execution) is meant.

issues.canonical: The start timer operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." start [ "(" TimerValue ")" ].
issues.original: ObjectReference "." start [ "(" ObjectReference ")" ]
issues.issue: The syntax block names the optional parenthesized argument 'ObjectReference' while the restrictions describe a SingleExpression giving the timer value.
readings: The optional argument of the start timer operation IS a SingleExpression giving the timer value.
The optional argument of the start timer operation IS an ObjectReference.

issues.canonical: When a timer is started, the timer IS added to the running-timer list.
issues.original: When a timer is started, its name is added to the list of running timers (for the given scope unit).
issues.issue: The sentence says the timer is added to the list 'for the given scope unit', while clause 23.1 says each component maintains one running-timer list.
readings: When a timer is started, the timer IS added to the running-timer list of the component.
When a timer is started, the timer IS added to a running-timer list specific to the scope unit.

issues.canonical: Starting a timer without a specified timer value SHALL cause a runtime error when the timer has no default duration.
issues.original: Starting a timer with a negative timer value, e.g. the timer value is the result of an expression, or without a specified timer value shall cause a runtime error.
issues.issue: Read literally, starting a timer 'without a specified timer value' always causes an error, which contradicts the use of the default duration (23.2-s004/s005).
readings: Starting a timer without a timer value SHALL cause a runtime error only if the timer has no default duration.
Starting a timer without a timer value SHALL always cause a runtime error.

issues.canonical: In an `any from` running timer operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.
issues.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and their states are checked individually, from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
issues.issue: 'from innermost to outermost dimension' does not state clearly which index varies fastest.
readings: The index of the innermost (last) dimension varies fastest, i.e. row-major order [0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1].
The innermost dimension is processed first as the slowest-varying index.

issues.canonical: If the index redirection of a running timer operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.
issues.original: d) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
issues.issue: 'dimension' is used for 'number of dimensions'.

issues.canonical: The timeout operation IS checking the expiration of a specific timer of the scope unit in which it is called, or of any timer started on the test component or control component before entering that scope.
issues.original: The timeout operation allows to check the expiration of a specific timer in the scope unit of a test component or control component in which the timeout operation has been called or of any timer that has been started on a test component or control component before entering the scope in which the timeout operation has been called.
issues.issue: The sentence lists two alternatives without stating which syntax form addresses which; it is unclear whether 'any timer' also covers timers that are not visible in the scope.
readings: `T.timeout` checks a timer visible in the scope unit, and `any timer.timeout` checks any timer started on the component, including timers not visible in the scope.
Both forms only check timers visible in the scope unit in which the timeout operation is called.

issues.canonical: In an `any from` timeout operation, the timers of the referenced timer array ARE checked individually for timeout, iterating from the innermost to the outermost dimension and from the lowest to the highest index in each dimension.
issues.original: When the any from `TimerArrayRef` notation is used, where TimerArrayRef shall be a timer array identifier, the timers from the referenced array are iterated over and individually checked for timeout from innermost to outermost dimension from lowest to highest index for each dimension.
issues.issue: 'from innermost to outermost dimension' does not state clearly which index varies fastest.
readings: The index of the innermost (last) dimension varies fastest, i.e. row-major order.
The innermost dimension is processed first as the slowest-varying index.

issues.canonical: If the index redirection of a timeout operation is used for a multi-dimensional timer array, the size of the integer array or record of integer type SHALL be exactly the number of dimensions of the timer array.
issues.original: e) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional timer arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective timer array, and its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the timer array.
issues.issue: 'dimension' is used for 'number of dimensions'.

issues.canonical: A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions.
issues.original: These operations shall only be used in test cases, altsteps and functions.
issues.issue: Chose reading 1: 'functions' means functions that execute on a test component; verdict operations are not meaningful in the module control function (no local verdict). Also 'test cases' denotes testcase definitions.
readings: A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions executed on a test component, and SHALL NOT be used in the module control function or in functions called from it.
A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions, including any function called from the module control function.

issues.canonical: A local verdict IS an entity owned by a single test component.
issues.original: The local verdict is an object which is created for each test component at the time of its creation.
issues.issue: 'object' is a glossary term for instances of classes (OO extension); the local verdict is not a class object.

issues.canonical: An `error` verdict IS only obtainable as the result of an `execute` operation.
issues.original: This means that an error verdict can only be a result of an execute test case operation.
issues.issue: Chose reading 1 (error appears only as the return value of execute, since it cannot be set or read inside test components). 'execute test case operation' is not the name of the operation.
readings: An `error` verdict IS only observable as the value returned by an `execute` operation.
An `error` verdict IS only produced while a testcase started by an `execute` operation is running.

issues.canonical: The implicit charstring variable CANNOT be retrieved or read by any TTCN-3 language construct.
issues.original: The implicit charstring variable cannot be retrieved and read by any TTCN-3 function, it only provides additional information for logging.
issues.issue: 'TTCN-3 function' is meant as any TTCN-3 language construct (statement, operation, predefined or user-defined function).

issues.canonical: A `setverdict` operation MAY have optional FreeText or TemplateInstance arguments providing information that explains the reasons for assigning the verdict.
issues.original: The optional parameters allow to provide information that explain the reasons for assigning the verdict.
issues.issue: 'optional parameters' refers to the optional FreeText/TemplateInstance arguments (actual parameters) of setverdict.

issues.canonical: The information given in the optional arguments of a `setverdict` operation IS composed into a single string.
issues.original: This information is composed to a string and stored in an implicit charstring variable.
issues.issue: The composition rule is not stated; chose reading 1 (as for log, cf. example 2 'Value received: 5').
readings: The optional arguments ARE concatenated without separators, each converted to text as the log statement does.
The optional arguments ARE composed into a string using an implementation-dependent format.

issues.canonical: The SingleExpression of a `setverdict` operation SHALL resolve to a value of type `verdicttype`.
issues.original: b) _SingleExpression shall resolve to a value of type verdict._
issues.issue: The type is named 'verdicttype', not 'verdict'.

issues.canonical: The `action` statement provides the means to write one or more items, e.g. to a displaying device.
issues.original: The action statement provides the means to write one or more log items e.g. to some displaying device.
issues.issue: The items of the action statement are called "log items" although they belong to the action statement, not the log statement.

issues.canonical: An item of the `action` statement MAY be an individual language element specified in table 18 or an expression composed of such items.
issues.original: Items may be individual language elements specified in table 18 or expressions composed of such items.
issues.issue: The syntax (25-s006) only allows FreeText or TemplateInstance, while table 18 (log statement) also lists elements such as timers, ports and component references; it is unclear whether all table 18 elements are allowed in `action`. Chosen reading: the elements of table 18 are allowed.
readings: An item of the `action` statement MAY be any language element listed in table 18 or an expression composed of such elements.
An item of the `action` statement MAY only be a free text or a template instance, as given by the syntactical structure.

issues.canonical: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions and altsteps.
issues.original: External actions can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
issues.issue: The list omits the module control function, although table 16 and clause 26 allow `action` in control behaviour. Chosen reading: the list is not exhaustive. Also "test cases" is used where "testcases" (the language element) is meant.
readings: The `action` statement MAY be used in testcases, functions, altsteps and the module control function.
The `action` statement MAY be used only in testcases, functions and altsteps.

issues.canonical: A test case IS executed by an `execute` statement in the module control function.
issues.original: Test cases are executed with an execute statement in the module control.
issues.issue: "module control" is used instead of the V4.17.1 term "module control function".

issues.canonical: The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case in control behaviour.
issues.original: The execute statement is used to start test cases (see clause 27.1) in control behaviour.
issues.issue: The cross-reference "see clause 27.1" points to the attribute mechanism, which is unrelated; clause 16.3 (Test cases) is most likely meant. The reading with clause 16.3 is used.
readings: The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case (as defined in clause 16.3) in control behaviour.
The `execute` statement IS used to start a test case in control behaviour, with attribute rules of clause 27.1 applying.

issues.canonical: A test component or port created or connected (by `create`, `connect`, etc. operations) in a previous test case IS destroyed when that test case is stopped and IS NOT visible to a subsequent test case.
issues.original: This means that all components and ports conducted by create, connect, etc. operations in a previous test case were destroyed when that test case was stopped (hence are not "visible" to the new test case).
issues.issue: "conducted" is used for components and ports set up by create/connect/map operations; "created" (components) and "connected/mapped" (ports) is meant.

issues.canonical: The MTC SHOULD ensure, by means of the `done` or `killed` operation, that all PTCs have stopped before it stops itself.
issues.original: NOTE 2: To avoid race conditions for the calculation of test verdicts due to the delayed stopping of PTCs, the MTC should ensure that all PTCs have stopped (by means of the done or killed statement) before it stops itself.
issues.issue: done and killed are called "statement" although the standard defines them as component operations.

issues.canonical: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
issues.original: This may be done using an explicit timeout in the execute statement.
issues.issue: "may" can be read as a permission (one possible way, others exist) or as a description of the only mechanism; the execute statement timeout is the only mechanism defined, so the descriptive reading is used.
readings: Test case supervision IS done by an explicit timeout (TimerValue) in the `execute` statement.
Test case supervision MAY be done by an explicit timeout in the `execute` statement or by other means.

issues.canonical: If the corresponding formal parameter is not of template kind, an actual parameter (TemplateInstance) of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to an expression.
issues.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.
issues.issue: The grammar symbol TemplateInstance is used where the actual parameter is meant (the syntax block uses ActualPar); "of template type" means a template formal parameter, not a type.

issues.canonical: The `execute` statement SHALL NOT be called from within a test behaviour called from a test case; a test case SHALL only be executed from control behaviour.
issues.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.
issues.issue: "executing test behaviour chain" is not a defined term; the call chain of functions and altsteps started by a test case (test behaviour) is meant.

issues.canonical: When the module control function is started, the test system creates a test component called control component.
issues.original: When the control function is started, the TE creates a test component called control component.
issues.issue: The abbreviation "TE" (TTCN-3 executable) is not defined in the core language; "test system" is the glossary term. "control function" means the module control function.

issues.canonical: If no program statements are used, test cases ARE executed by default in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.
issues.original: If no programming statements are used then, by default, the test cases are executed in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.
issues.issue: The module control function needs execute statements, so "no programming statements" most likely means no control-flow statements; reading chosen: execute statements without control-flow statements run in textual order.
readings: If the module control function contains no control-flow statements, its `execute` statements ARE executed in textual order.
If the module control function contains no statements other than test case references, the referenced test cases ARE executed in textual order.

issues.canonical: A `with` statement MAY be applied to a module, to a global module definition, and to a local definition in the module control function, in a test case, in a function, in an altstep, in a statement block or in a component type definition.
issues.original: The with statement can be applied to modules, global module definitions and to local definitions in control, test cases, functions, altsteps, statement blocks and in component type definitions.
issues.issue: 'control' is used for the module control function; the outdated term 'control part' is implied.

issues.canonical: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override the outer `with` statement.
issues.original: A with statement that is placed inside the scope of another with statement shall override the outermost with.
issues.issue: 'the outermost with' can be read literally (only the outermost of several nested with statements) or as 'any enclosing with'. The second reading is chosen because the nested overriding scheme of example 2 implies it.
readings: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override every enclosing `with` statement.
A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override only the outermost `with` statement.

issues.canonical: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of the attributes of that kind, unless specified otherwise.
issues.original: If multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them are overridden unless specified otherwise.
issues.issue: 'unless specified otherwise' does not say where the exception is specified (e.g. clause 27.1.2.2 for multiple encodings); 'type' is used for the kind of attribute. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, except where another clause of the standard specifies a different rule.
If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, unless the overriding attribute definition itself specifies otherwise.

issues.canonical: An attribute from a higher scope IS affecting the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to a scope between them.
issues.original: Attributes from higher scope will still affect attributes in lower scopes even if the @local attribute is between them.
issues.issue: 'affect attributes in lower scopes' is read as affecting the language elements of lower scopes (they inherit the higher-scope attribute), not as modifying explicit lower-scope attributes.
readings: An attribute from a higher scope IS applied to the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.
An attribute from a higher scope IS overriding explicitly declared attributes in lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.

issues.canonical: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
issues.original: The override directive overrides the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
issues.issue: The sentence seems to conflict with 27.1.2.0-s022, which states that the override directive overwrites attribute definitions of lower scopes.
