issues.issue: The statement restates a property that every octetstring value has by definition (one octet is two hexadecimal digits), so it is unclear whether it is a restriction with an observable error case or merely explanatory.
readings: The number of hexadecimal digits of the octetstring value passed to `oct2int` IS always a multiple of 2, since every octetstring value consists of whole octets.
An `invalue` argument of `oct2int` with an odd number of hexadecimal digits SHALL cause an error.

issues.canonical: The hexstring value returned by `oct2hex` SHALL contain the same sequence of hex digits as the input octetstring value.
issues.original: For the purpose of this conversion, a octetstring shall be converted into a hexstring containing the same sequence of hex digits as the octetstring.
issues.issue: Uses the article 'a' before 'octetstring'.

issues.canonical: The predefined function `oct2str` converts the octetstring value `invalue` to a charstring value representing the string equivalent of the input value.
issues.original: This function converts an octetstring `invalue to an charstring representing the string equivalent of the` input value.
issues.issue: 'String equivalent' could mean the hexadecimal-digit text of the octets or the character interpretation of the octets; the following sentences and the example show the hexadecimal-digit text is meant (the character interpretation is oct2char).
readings: The predefined function `oct2str` converts the octetstring value to a charstring value consisting of the characters of its hexadecimal digits.
The predefined function `oct2str` converts the octetstring value to a charstring value whose characters are the octets interpreted as character codes.

issues.canonical: The charstring value returned by `oct2str` SHALL have the same length as the input octetstring value.
issues.original: The resulting charstring shall have the same length as the incoming octetstring.
issues.issue: The length of an octetstring is counted in octets, but each octet yields two characters (see C.1.24-s004 and the example where '4469707379'O, 5 octets, gives a 10-character charstring), so 'same length' contradicts the conversion rule unless length means the number of hex digits.
readings: The charstring value returned by `oct2str` SHALL have twice as many characters as the input octetstring value has octets (i.e. one character per hex digit).
The charstring value returned by `oct2str` SHALL have as many characters as the input octetstring value has octets.

issues.canonical: The `invalue` argument of `oct2char` SHALL NOT contain octet values higher than 7F.
issues.original: The input parameter invalue shall not` contain octet values higher than 7F.
issues.issue: The text does not say whether a violation causes an error (and whether at compile time or runtime); the error-cause list refers only to the general causes of 16.1.2.
readings: An `invalue` argument of `oct2char` containing an octet value higher than 7F SHALL cause an error.
The behaviour of `oct2char` for an `invalue` argument containing an octet value higher than 7F IS undefined.

issues.canonical: If `invalue` contains an odd number of characters, the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` contains the hex digit 0 as leftmost digit followed by the same sequence of characters as in the charstring value.
issues.original: When the string invalue contains even number characters the resulting octetstring contains 0 as leftmost character followed by the same sequence of characters as in the charstring.
issues.issue: The text says 'even number characters', but the example str2oct("1D7") = '01D7'O and the parallel rule of hex2oct show that an odd number of characters is meant; the case of an even number (no padding) is not stated explicitly.
readings: If `invalue` contains an odd number of characters, the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` contains 0 as leftmost hex digit followed by the characters of `invalue`.
If `invalue` contains an even number of characters, the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` contains 0 as leftmost hex digit followed by the characters of `invalue`.

issues.canonical: `lengthof` applied to the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` returns half of `lengthof` of the input charstring value.
issues.original: **lengthof (see clause C.2.1 for the resulting octetstring) will return half of lengthof of the incoming charstring.
issues.issue: For an input with an odd number of characters the result is padded, so the length is half the input length rounded up (e.g. "1D7" gives 2 octets); the text does not mention rounding. The sentence is also garbled by bold markup in the PDF conversion.
readings: `lengthof` applied to the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` returns the length of the input charstring value divided by 2, rounded up.
`lengthof` applied to the octetstring value returned by `str2oct` returns exactly half of the length of the input charstring value, which is only defined for inputs of even length.

issues.canonical: The number in decimal notation in the `invalue` argument of `str2float` MAY have no digits after the dot.
issues.original: no numbers after the dot in the decimal notation are allowed.
issues.issue: 'no numbers after the dot ... are allowed' can be read as a permission (digits after the dot may be omitted) or as a prohibition (digits after the dot are forbidden); the example "+001." and "12345.6" show the permission is meant. Also 'numbers' is used where 'digits' is meant.
readings: The number in decimal notation in the `invalue` argument of `str2float` MAY have no digits after the dot.
The number in decimal notation in the `invalue` argument of `str2float` SHALL NOT have digits after the dot.

issues.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` parameter of `enum2int` SHALL always be a typed object.
issues.original: The actual parameter passed to inpar always shall be a typed object (see clause 6.2.4 and the definition "type context" in clause 3.1).
issues.issue: 'typed object' is not defined in clause 3.1; the sentence refers to the glossary term 'type context', so the intended meaning is an enumerated value whose type is known from its context or a type prefix.

issues.canonical: The octetstring returned by `unichar2oct` SHALL contain the octets mandated by mapping the characters of `invalue` with the standardized mapping associated with the given `string_encoding`, in the same order as the characters appear in `invalue`.
issues.original: Each octet of the octetstring` will contain the octets mandated by mapping the characters of invalue using the standardized mapping associated with the given string_encoding in the same order as the characters appear in inpar.
issues.issue: The sentence refers to the parameter 'inpar', which does not exist in the signature of unichar2oct; 'invalue' is meant.

issues.canonical: The universal charstring resulting from `any2unistr` IS the same as the string produced by the `log` operation containing the same operand as the one passed to `any2unistr`.
issues.original: The resulting universal charstring is the same as the string produced by the log operation containing the same operand as the one passed to the any2unistr function.
issues.issue: The unconditional statement conflicts with the format-dependent rules of C.1.33-s007/s008; the second reading (default behaviour) was chosen as consistent with the rest of the clause, but the canonical text keeps the unconditional wording of the source.
readings: The result of any2unistr IS always the same as the string produced by the log operation for the same operand.
The result of any2unistr IS the same as the string produced by the log operation for the same operand only when the format parameter is missing or empty.

issues.canonical: The value or template passed to the `invalue` parameter of `any2unistr` MAY be uninitialized, partially initialized or completely initialized.
issues.original: The value or template passed as a parameter to the any2unichar function may be uninitialized, partially or completely initialized.
issues.issue: The sentence names the function 'any2unichar', which does not exist; 'any2unistr' is meant.

issues.canonical: When the `format` parameter of `any2unistr` is "canonical", unbound fields SHALL be represented in the output as "-".
issues.original: When the optional format parameter takes the value "canonical": unbound fields are represented in the output as "-", the fields and members of structured types are represented recursively in assignment notation.
issues.issue: 'unbound' is not a TTCN-3 term; the glossary uses 'uninitialized'. The example shows that a completely uninitialized template is also represented as "-".

issues.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a string-type template, `inpar` SHALL only contain the matching mechanisms specific value, template list, complemented template list, pattern, "?" (AnyValue), "*" (AnyValueOrNone), combined template and the length restriction matching attribute.
issues.original: When the function lengthof is applied to string-type templates, inpar shall only contain the following matching mechanisms: specific value, value list, complemented value list, pattern, "?" (AnyValue instead of value), "*" (AnyValueOrNone instead of value), combined template and the length restriction matching attribute.
issues.issue: Clauses B.1.2.1 and B.1.2.2 name these matching mechanisms 'template list' and 'complemented template list'.

issues.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a string-type template, `inpar` SHALL match values of the same length only, with the exception of specific values and patterns.
issues.original: In case of stringtype templates inpar shall match values of the same length only with the exception of specific values and patterns.
issues.issue: It is unclear what the exception exempts; the examples ('1*F'H causes an error, '00*FF'O length(1..2) returns 2) suggest that patterns with '*' still need a determinable length. The first reading follows the wording and was chosen.
readings: A string-type template passed to lengthof SHALL match values of one length only, unless it is a specific value or a pattern, which MAY match values of different lengths.
A string-type template passed to lengthof SHALL match values of one length only; for specific values and patterns only the counting rule of clause 15.6.1 differs.

issues.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a template of a record of or set of type, `inpar` SHALL only contain the matching mechanisms specific value, template list, complemented template list, "?" (AnyValue), "*" (AnyValueOrNone), SuperSet, SubSet, combined template, permutation and the length restriction matching attribute.

(AnyValue instead of value), "*" (AnyValueOrNone instead of value), SuperSet, SubSet, combined template, permutation and the length restriction matching attribute.
issues.issue: Clauses B.1.2.1 and B.1.2.2 name these matching mechanisms 'template list' and 'complemented template list'.

issues.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with an argument that is not of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of or array SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: the template passed to the invalue parameter is not of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, or array.

readings: Calling lengthof with an argument not of a string, record of, set of, array or map type SHALL cause an error (map is allowed, as stated in C.2.1-s002/s006).

issues.canonical: Calling `sizeof` with an argument that is not of a record or set type SHALL cause an error.
issues.original: the template passed to the inpar parameter is not of a record or set type.

issues.canonical: If the `@nocase` modifier is present in a `regexp` call, the matching of that call SHALL be done in a case-insensitive way as specified in clause B.1.5.6.
issues.original: If the @nocase modifier is present, this and all subsequent matchings shall be done in a case-insensitive way, as specified in clause B.1.5.6.

issues.original: In case inpar is a template, it shall contain the specific value matching mechanism only.

readings: If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value matching mechanism only.
If inpar of `regexp` is a template, it SHALL contain the specific value or character pattern matching mechanism only.

readings: An error SHALL occur if inpar is a template containing a matching mechanism other than specific value or character pattern.

issues.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` is of a binary string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a specific value containing as many AnyElement symbols as the count parameter.
issues.original: A specific value containing as many AnyElement symbols as is the count parameter is returned if the referenced template if of a binary string type and contains the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol.
issues.issue: Typo "template if of a binary string type" should read "template is of a binary string type".

issues.canonical: If the referenced template of `substr` is of a character string type and contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, `substr` SHALL return a pattern containing as many ? metacharacters as the count parameter.
issues.original: A pattern containing as many ? metacharacters as is the count parameter is returned if the referenced template if of a character string type and contains the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol.
issues.issue: Typo "template if of a character string type" should read "template is of a character string type".

issues.canonical: If inpar of `substr` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `substr` SHALL have the present restriction.
issues.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.

issues.canonical: When inpar of `substr` is a template of a sequence type or an array, it SHALL contain only specific values, AnyElement or combined templates whose elements are specific values, AnyElement or combined templates.
issues.original: When inpar is a template of sequence type or is an array, only the specific value combined templates whose elements are specific values, and AnyElement matching mechanisms or combined templates are allowed and the substring or subsequence to be returned shall not contain AnyElement or combined template.

readings: inpar SHALL contain only specific values, AnyElement, or combined templates whose elements are specific values, AnyElement or combined templates.
inpar SHALL be a specific value or a combined template whose elements are only specific values, AnyElement or combined templates (AnyElement not allowed at the top level).

issues.canonical: The `replace` function SHALL replace the substring or subsequence of inpar starting at index index with length len by repl and return the resulting string or sequence.
issues.original: This function replaces the substring or subsequence of value inpar at index index of length len with the string or sequence value repl and returns the resulting string or sequence.
issues.issue: "value inpar" and "sequence value repl" although C.4.3-s011/s013 allow templates for both parameters.

readings: If inpar or repl contains a template, the returned template SHALL always have the present restriction.

issues.canonical: In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a binary string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone.
issues.original: In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type
issues.issue: The lead-in says "if any of the following conditions is met" but the following items are conversion targets with conditions attached; the first reading is chosen.
readings: AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted to a binary string with a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type.
AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted only if some further unstated condition is met, the listed items being the conditions.

issues.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the present restriction.
issues.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.
issues.issue: Garbled sentence with unclear scope of "a reference to"; the three-alternative reading is chosen.
readings: The returned value SHALL have the present restriction if inpar contains (a) a reference to a template with the present restriction, (b) a matching symbol fulfilling the present restriction, or (c) a reference to an unrestricted template field representing a mandatory record/set field or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array.
The returned value SHALL have the present restriction only if inpar contains a reference to a present-restricted template whose content is such a matching symbol or field reference.

issues.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
issues.original:
When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send
statement). The returned bitstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not
make any check on its correctness. The optional encoding_info parameter is used for passing additional encoding
information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value
for this single encvalue call. The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

  - Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).

issues.canonical: The octet serialization of the characters used by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
issues.original: The serialized bitstring shall not include the optional signature (see clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2], also known as byte order mark).
issues.issue: 'The serialized bitstring' is not a parameter or result of `encvalue_unichar` (which handles a universal charstring); it is unclear which bit/octet sequence must be free of the BOM. The first reading (the intermediate octet serialization) was chosen.
readings: The octet serialization of the characters used by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
The `encvalue_unichar` function SHALL NOT produce or expect a byte order mark in the bitstring exchanged with the codec.
The universal charstring handled by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT start with the character U+FEFF.

issues.canonical: A call encvalue_unichar(inpar, string_serialization, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding) IS equivalent to oct2unichar(bit2oct(encvalue(inpar, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding)), string_serialization).
issues.issue: The explanatory definition names the serialization parameter `enc` (without default "UTF-8" and with a missing comma), while the signature in C.5.3-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

issues.canonical: The `string_serialization` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS the definition of how the encoded octets (the encoded bitstring received from the codec) contain the characters.
issues.original: The string_serialization parameter defines how the encoded octets (in fact the encoded bitstring received from the codec) contain the characters.

issues.canonical: A call of `encvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error when the given string encoding (`string_serialization`) is not recognized.
issues.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: The given string encoding is not recognized.

issues.issue: 'can be assigned' and the position of `bit_length` after defaulted parameters leave open whether the actual parameter may be omitted; out parameters have no default value, so the mandatory reading was chosen.

issues.original: The identified encoding scheme, or the value "<unknown>", if the type of encoding cannot be determined unanimously, shall be returned as a character string.

readings: `hostid` SHALL return the empty string if no host id of the kind given by `idkind` can be retrieved.
`hostid` SHALL return the empty string if no host id of a kind different from `idkind` can be retrieved.

issues.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template (e.g. a pattern string).
issues.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.
issues.issue: "templates" is ambiguous: D.5 examples (D.5-s014) show __SCOPE__ being replaced in template definitions, so "templates" most likely means literal character string templates such as pattern strings. The canonical text chooses that reading.
readings: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template such as a pattern string.
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced anywhere inside a template definition.

issues.canonical: The basic scope units of TTCN-3 ARE the module definitions part, the module control function, component types, functions, altsteps, testcases, statement blocks, templates and user-defined named types.
issues.original: According to clause 5.2, basic scope units of TTCN-3 are module definitions part, module control function, component types, functions, altsteps, test cases, statement blocks, templates and user defined named types.
issues.issue: Uses "test cases" and "user defined named types"; elsewhere the standard uses the keyword-style "testcase" and the glossary term "user-defined type".

issues.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__SCOPE__` with a charstring value determined by the kind of the lowest named scope unit.
issues.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __SCOPE__ with a charstring value which includes:
issues.issue: "a charstring value which includes" could mean the value consists exactly of the listed name or merely contains it. The examples (D.5-s014) show the value equals the name, so the canonical requirements in items a) to h) use "equal to".
readings: The replacement charstring value SHALL be exactly the listed name.
The replacement charstring value SHALL contain the listed name, possibly with additional text.

issues.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is an altstep definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the altstep name as a charstring value.
issues.original: e) an altstep name, if the lowest named scope is an altstep definition;
issues.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit" as in items a) to d).

issues.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a function definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the function name as a charstring value.
issues.original: f) a function name, if the lowest named scope is a function definition;
issues.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit".

issues.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a local or global template definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the template name as a charstring value.
issues.original: g) a template name, if the lowest named scope is a template definition (local or global); or h) the type name, if the lowest named scope is a user defined named type definition.
issues.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit".

issues.canonical: If the lowest named scope unit is a user-defined named type definition, a preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace `__SCOPE__` with the type name as a charstring value.
issues.original: g) a template name, if the lowest named scope is a template definition (local or global); or h) the type name, if the lowest named scope is a user defined named type definition.
issues.issue: Uses "lowest named scope" instead of "lowest named scope unit" and "user defined named type" instead of the glossary term "user-defined type".
